The side-necked turtles, by contrast, occur only in the southern hemisphere and in the tropics. In Europe, therefore, only hidden-necked turtles live.

Tortoises eat mainly plants such as herbs, grasses and flowers. Pond turtles hunt worms, snails, insects, tadpoles and small fish. All turtles lay their eggs on land, often in a pit that they dig themselves. In regions with cold winters, many species go into **winter torpor**.

The **European pond turtle** is the only native turtle in Switzerland. It has become very rare and is being reintroduced in some areas with conservation projects. Released pets such as the red-eared slider from North America live in some waters and can harm native animals. Popular as a pet is the Hermann's tortoise, which needs a lot of space outdoors.

begriffe.erklaerung: The scientific name of the hidden-necked turtles, meaning roughly “hidden neck”.
Turtles that fold their neck sideways under the edge of the shell.
The hard casing of the turtle made up of the upper shield and the lower shield.
A state in winter in which cold-blooded animals hardly move and eat nothing.

gewusst: Sea turtles are hidden-necked turtles, but can hardly pull their heads into the shell any more.
Giant tortoises can live to well over 100 years old.
In many turtles, the temperature in the nest decides whether a male or a female hatches from an egg.

teile.einleitung: The nasturtium is a popular garden and balcony plant with bright orange, yellow or red flowers. It comes from South America and is edible: the flowers and leaves taste peppery like cress. Gardeners also use it as a helper against aphids.
wichtigste: The nasturtium comes from the Andes in South America.
Its flowers are orange, yellow or red and have a long spur.
The leaves and flowers are edible and taste peppery.
It attracts aphids and so lures them away from other plants.
Here it is usually an annual, because it cannot tolerate frost.
Its German name comes from the shape of the flower, which is reminiscent of a monk’s hood.
It is also used as a medicinal plant.

abschnitte.text: The best-known species is the **garden nasturtium**. Its leaves are almost perfectly round like small shields, and the stalk is attached in the middle. The flowers have five petals and, at the back, a long, pointed **spur** that holds sweet nectar. The plant can creep along the ground or climb several metres high.

Nasturtiums come from Central and South America, above all from the Andes, for example in Peru. Spanish sailors brought them to Europe in the 16th century. Because they flower so beautifully, they quickly became popular in gardens. The German name recalls the hood of the **Capuchin friars**.

The nasturtium strongly attracts **aphids**. That is why gardeners like to plant it next to vegetables, fruit trees or roses, so that the aphids prefer to go to the nasturtium. Such a plant is called a **trap plant**. The caterpillars of the large white butterfly also like to feed on it.

The leaves and flowers of the nasturtium taste peppery and spicy, rather like garden cress or mustard. **Mustard oils** are responsible for this; the plant makes them to protect itself. You can sprinkle the flowers colourfully over salads and pickle the green seeds like capers. Because mustard oils work against germs, the plant is also used in herbal medicine.

On the leaves of the nasturtium, drops of water bead up and roll off like little balls. As they do so they pick up dust and dirt, so the leaves stay clean. This is called the **lotus effect**, after the lotus flower, which does it especially well. Researchers use this as a model for self-cleaning surfaces.

In its South American home, hummingbirds also visit the flowers. Here it is mainly bumblebees that fetch the nectar from the long spur. The nasturtium likes to grow in sunny places and flowers from early summer until the first **frost**. In Switzerland you often see it on balconies and in cottage gardens.

begriffe.erklaerung: A long, tube-shaped pouch on the flower that holds nectar.
A plant that attracts pests and so protects other plants.
A sharp-tasting substance in plants such as mustard, cress and radish.
Water beads off a surface and takes dirt with it.

gewusst: The nasturtium is not related to garden cress; it just tastes similar.
In Germany the nasturtium was chosen as medicinal plant of the year 2013.

teile.einleitung: The golden jackal is a slim wild dog with golden-yellow fur. It is bigger than a fox, but clearly smaller than a wolf. For some years now it has been spreading in Europe and has even reached Switzerland.
wichtigste: Like the wolf and the fox, the golden jackal belongs to the dog family.
Its fur is mostly golden yellow to greyish brown.
It lives in parts of Europe, Asia and North Africa.
It is an opportunist and eats whatever it can find.
Both parents look after the pups together.
With howling, jackals keep in contact and mark their territory.
In Switzerland it was first observed in 2011 and is protected here.

abschnitte.text: The golden jackal is called **Canis aureus** in science, which means golden dog. Without its tail it grows to about 70 to 105 centimetres long, stands about 40 to 50 centimetres high at the shoulder and weighs up to about 15 kilograms. That makes it clearly smaller than a wolf. The fur is golden yellow to greyish brown, and the tail is rather short with a dark tip. The males are usually somewhat bigger than the females.

The golden jackal occurs in parts of Europe, Asia and North Africa, for example in South-East Europe, in Turkey, in the Middle East and in India. It likes open landscapes with bushes, reeds and fields. For some decades it has been moving north and west from the **Balkans** and has now reached as far as Austria, Germany and Switzerland. The jackals in Africa are now regarded by some experts as a species of their own, the African golden wolf.

The golden jackal is an **opportunist**, which means that it adapts its food to what is on offer. It eats mice, birds, insects, lizards, fruit and also carrion. It hunts alone, in pairs or in small groups. Sometimes it takes lambs or poultry, so it occasionally comes into conflict with farmers. Because it eats many mice, however, it is also useful to agriculture.

Golden jackals mostly live as a **pair**, which often stays together for a long time. After a pregnancy of about two months, several pups are born, often three to six. They are blind and helpless at birth and grow up in a burrow. Both parents look after the young and bring them food. With loud **howling**, the jackals keep in contact with each other and show whose territory it is.

In Switzerland the golden jackal was first observed in 2011. In the winter of 2011/12 it walked into **camera traps** in the cantons of Bern, Vaud and Fribourg that had actually been set up for lynxes. Since then there have been repeated sightings from various cantons. In Switzerland the golden jackal is protected by the **hunting law** and may not be hunted. Because it is shy, you only rarely get to see it.

begriffe.erklaerung: An animal that eats whatever is easy to get at the time.
The area that an animal or an animal family defends as its home.
A camera in the woods that automatically takes a picture when an animal goes past.
What young dogs, wolves, foxes or jackals are called.

gewusst: Young golden jackals sometimes help for a year with raising their younger siblings.
On its travels, a single jackal can cover hundreds of kilometres to find a new territory.
Even in ancient Egypt people knew jackal-like dogs, and the god Anubis was shown with a dog's head.

teile.einleitung: The cashmere goat is a goat with an especially fine, soft undercoat. From this wool, cashmere, cosy and warm jumpers, scarves and hats are made. The animals live mainly in the cold highlands of Asia.
wichtigste: The cashmere goat is known for its especially fine wool.
Its soft undercoat is used for warm jumpers.
The name comes from the region of Kashmir in the Himalayas.
Today most cashmere goats live in China and Mongolia.
The wool is combed out in spring, when the goats shed their winter coat.
One goat yields only a little fine wool a year.
Cashmere is therefore expensive and valuable.

abschnitte.text: Cashmere goats are medium-sized goats with horns and a coat of two layers. On the outside grow long, coarse **guard hairs** that protect against rain and wind. Underneath lies a very fine, soft **undercoat** that keeps warm like a down jacket. Depending on the breed, the coat is white, grey, brown or black.

The name comes from **Kashmir**, a region in the Himalayas between India and Pakistan. Cashmere goats live in cold, dry highlands with icy winters. Today most come from China, especially from Inner Mongolia, and from Mongolia. There, nomads keep large herds on wide steppes.

A cashmere hair is much thinner than a human hair, usually thinner than 19 thousandths of a millimetre. In spring the goats shed their winter coat, and then the undercoat is combed out or sheared. One goat yields only about 100 to 200 grams of pure **cashmere wool** a year. For one jumper you therefore need the wool of several goats.

Jumpers, scarves, hats and blankets are made from cashmere. The wool is very light and soft and still keeps you warm. As early as the 18th and 19th centuries, **cashmere shawls** from India were in great demand in Europe. Because the wool is rare, cashmere is one of the most expensive natural fibres.

Cashmere goats eat grasses, herbs, leaves and twigs. They are undemanding and manage on poor food. Goats, however, often tear plants out roots and all. Because the number of goats in Mongolia has risen sharply, many pastures are **overgrazed**.

Where too many goats graze, the soil can dry out and turn into desert, which is called **desertification**. That is why some manufacturers pay attention to sustainable sourcing of the wool. In Switzerland there are only a few cashmere goats, kept by some hobby breeders. Here other goat breeds such as the Saanen goat are much more common.

begriffe.erklaerung: Fine, soft hairs under the coarse coat that keep the animal warm.
Long, coarse hairs of the outer layer of the coat.
People who move from place to place with their herds.
When too many animals eat a pasture bare.

gewusst: Cashmere wool keeps you many times warmer than sheep’s wool of the same weight.
Mongolia has many more goats than inhabitants.

teile.einleitung: The greenshank is a slender wader with long, greenish legs. It breeds in the bogs of the north and rests on its migration to Africa also at Swiss lakes. Its bright, three-syllable call is typical and can be heard from far away.
wichtigste: The legs of the greenshank are mostly greenish, hence its name.
It belongs to the snipe family and is a wader.
Its long bill is curved slightly upwards.
It breeds in Northern Europe and Northern Asia, above all in bogs of the taiga.
In winter it moves as far as Africa, Southern Europe and Southern Asia.
In Switzerland you can see it as a passage migrant in spring and autumn.
Its call sounds like a clear, three-fold “tyoo tyoo tyoo”.

abschnitte.text: The greenshank is called **Tringa nebularia** in science and is about 30 to 35 centimetres long. It is patterned grey on top and white on the belly. Typical are the long, greenish legs and the long bill curved slightly upwards. In flight you see a white wedge on the back. It is somewhat larger than its relative the common redshank, which has bright red legs.

The greenshank breeds in the north of Europe and Asia, for example in Scotland, Scandinavia and Siberia. There it lives in **bogs** and open woods of the **taiga**. In late summer it moves south and spends the winter on coasts and lakes in the Mediterranean region, in Africa south of the Sahara or in Southern Asia. On the way it takes rests at bodies of water to feed.

The greenshank wades through shallow water and looks for insects, larvae, small crustaceans, worms and snails. Sometimes it also runs through the shallow water and hunts small fish. As it does, it probes and pecks with its long bill. On its migration it depends on mudflats and shallow shores where it finds enough food.

The nest is a simple hollow on the ground, often next to a stone or tree stump. The female usually lays four well-camouflaged eggs. Both parents incubate and afterwards lead the chicks, which look for food themselves shortly after hatching. Such young birds are called **precocial**. In danger the parents call loudly and fly around the intruder.

In Switzerland the greenshank does not breed, but it is a regular **passage migrant**. In April and May and from July to October it rests on lake shores, river deltas and gravel pits. Good places to watch it are protected areas such as the Fanel on Lake Neuchâtel or the Bolle di Magadino on Lake Maggiore. Such resting places with shallow shores and mudflats are very important for migratory birds.

begriffe.erklaerung: A long-legged bird that looks for food in shallow water.
A migratory bird that only passes through a country on its journey and rests briefly.
The huge belt of coniferous forest in the north of Europe, Asia and America.
A young bird that leaves the nest shortly after hatching.

gewusst: In summer the plumage of the greenshank is more darkly spotted, and in winter it looks much paler and greyer.
Greenshanks can cover thousands of kilometres on their migration.

teile.einleitung: The rooster is the tenth of the twelve animals in the Chinese zodiac. Every year in the Chinese calendar is dedicated to an animal, and in the Year of the Rooster the rooster is in the centre. The next Year of the Rooster begins in February 2029.
wichtigste: The Chinese zodiac consists of twelve animals that take turns each year.
The rooster is the tenth animal, after the monkey and before the dog.
Years of the Rooster were, for example, 1993, 2005 and 2017, and the next is 2029.
The Chinese year does not begin on 1 January, but between the end of January and mid-February.
Each animal is joined by one of five elements, so a cycle of 60 years arises.
According to tradition, the rooster is said to stand for diligence, punctuality and honesty.
The zodiac is also known in countries such as Vietnam, Korea and Japan.

abschnitte.titel: What is the Year of the Rooster?
abschnitte.text: In the **Chinese zodiac**, every year belongs to one of twelve animals. The order is: rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, **rooster**, dog and pig. After twelve years the series begins again from the start. Anyone born in a Year of the Rooster has the rooster as their animal sign, according to this tradition.

abschnitte.titel: When is the Year of the Rooster?
abschnitte.text: Years of the Rooster were, among others, 1981, 1993, 2005 and 2017. The next begins in February 2029. The Chinese year follows the **lunar calendar** and begins with the New Year festival between 21 January and 20 February. Anyone born on 20 January 2017, for example, therefore still belongs to the Year of the Monkey.

In the Chinese calendar, each animal is also linked with one of five **elements**: wood, fire, earth, metal and water. So 2017 was a year of the Fire Rooster. From twelve animals and five elements arises a cycle of **60 years**. Only after 60 years does exactly the same combination come round again.

abschnitte.titel: The legend of the great race
abschnitte.text: A well-known legend tells that the **Jade Emperor** invited the animals to a race across a river. The order in which they arrived determined their place in the calendar. The rooster is said to have crossed the river on a raft together with the monkey and the dog. The rat won because it rode along on the back of the ox and jumped off shortly before the finish.

The **Chinese New Year festival**, also called the Spring Festival, is the most important festival in China. It is celebrated with family meals, red envelopes of luck, fireworks and dragon dances. In Switzerland, too, many people with Chinese roots celebrate this festival. The characteristics of the animal signs are tradition and folk belief, and nothing about a person can be read from them scientifically.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fixed series of animals assigned to particular years.
A calendar in which the months follow the phases of the moon.
In the Chinese calendar, one of five basic forces such as fire or water.
Another name for the Chinese New Year festival.

gewusst: In the Chinese calendar, each animal is also assigned a time of day, and for the rooster it is the hours from 5 to 7 in the evening.
The rooster is the only bird among the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.
Anyone who reaches 60 experiences, in the Chinese calendar, exactly the same year as at their birth for the first time again.

teile.einleitung: Moulting is the process by which an animal sheds its outer covering once it has become too tight. This is necessary in insects, spiders, crustaceans and reptiles so that they can grow. What is left behind is often an empty shell that looks exactly like the animal.
wichtigste: In moulting, the animal sheds its outer covering that has become too tight.
Arthropods such as insects, spiders, woodlice and millipedes have to moult in order to grow.
Snakes and lizards such as the slow worm also moult.
The shell left behind is called an exuvia.
Directly after moulting, the animal is soft and vulnerable.
In insects, moulting is controlled by hormones.
A praying mantis usually hangs upside down from a support when moulting.

abschnitte.text: Insects, spiders, crustaceans and millipedes have a hard **exoskeleton** that cannot grow with them. To get bigger, they have to cast off the old covering and form a new, larger one. A woodlouse therefore moults several times in its life, even in two halves one after the other. In the grasshopper, it is said to moult before it reaches the next larval stage. Without moulting, these animals could not grow.

First the animal forms a new, still soft skin under the old covering. In insects this is controlled by the hormone **ecdysone**. Then the old covering usually splits open along the back and the animal slowly squeezes its way out. A praying mantis hangs upside down from a support while doing so, so that gravity helps. Afterwards the animal pumps air or fluid into its body so that the new covering becomes large before it hardens.

Snakes and lizards also moult, because their **scaly skin** does not grow with them. In a growing grass snake, the skin is shed regularly, often in a single piece, the **snake slough**. Beforehand their eyes become cloudy and bluish, because the skin over the eyes comes loose as well. Lizards such as the slow worm or wall lizards often lose their skin in shreds. Young, fast-growing animals moult more often than old ones.

Directly after moulting, the animal is soft and can hardly protect itself. Many animals therefore hide during this time. Crustaceans with a soft shell are called **soft-shell crabs**, and they are easy prey for predators. If something goes wrong during the moult, the animal can get stuck and die. Insects such as dragonflies therefore often moult early in the morning or at night.

The empty covering is called an **exuvia**. You can find, for example, dragonfly exuviae on reed stalks at the pond or old spider skins in the cellar. They look so like the animal that you can easily mistake them for a dead animal. Researchers use exuviae to determine which species of dragonfly live at a body of water. Humans too constantly lose tiny flakes of skin, but never the whole skin at once.

begriffe.erklaerung: The empty covering that is left behind after a moult.
A hard outer body covering that protects the animal like armour.
The shed skin of a snake.
A stage of development of a larva between two moults.

gewusst: Many amphibians eat their old skin after moulting.
Tarantulas can still moult even as adults and in doing so regrow lost legs.
When moulting, an insect even sheds the lining of its foregut and its breathing tubes.

teile.einleitung: The capped gibbon is a small ape from the rainforests of South-East Asia. It gets its name from the dark cap that the females wear on their pale heads. Like all gibbons, it swings elegantly from branch to branch and sings loud songs.
wichtigste: The capped gibbon lives in Thailand, Cambodia and Laos.
It belongs to the gibbons, which are also called lesser apes.
Males are black, females pale with a dark cap and dark chest.
It moves through the trees by swinging on its arms.
Pairs sing duets together in the morning.
It eats mainly ripe fruit.
The capped gibbon is endangered.

abschnitte.text: Capped gibbons have very long arms, a slender body and, like all apes, **no tail**. The males are almost entirely black, with white hands, feet and a white ring around the face. The females have pale, greyish-beige fur with a black **cap** on the head and a dark patch on the chest. An adult capped gibbon weighs only a few kilograms.

The capped gibbon lives in the south-east of Thailand, in Cambodia and in the south-west of Laos. There it inhabits evergreen **rainforests** and damp forests. It spends almost its whole life high up in the treetops. It only rarely comes down to the ground.

Gibbons move using a special technique, **brachiation**. They hang from their arms and swing from branch to branch as if on a climbing frame. In this way they cover several metres in one swing. Gibbons are among the fastest and most skilful climbers among the apes.

Capped gibbons live in small family groups made up of a pair and their young. Every morning the male and female sing a loud **duet** together that can be heard far through the forest. With it they show other gibbons that this territory is taken. The female usually gives birth to a single young one every two to three years.

Capped gibbons eat mainly ripe, sweet fruit such as figs. Added to this are young leaves, flowers and sometimes insects. Because they pass seeds in their droppings in other places, they help spread the forest. That is why they are also called **seed dispersers**.

The capped gibbon is **endangered**. Its forests are cut down for fields, plantations and timber. In addition, young animals are caught and sold illegally as pets. Capped gibbons still live in protected areas such as Khao Yai National Park in Thailand.

begriffe.erklaerung: A small ape from South-East Asia with very long arms.
A way of moving in which an ape swings from branch to branch on its arms.
A song that two sing together.
Dense forest in warm regions where it rains a great deal.

gewusst: In capped gibbons, males and females look so different that you could take them for two species.
The song of a gibbon pair can often be heard more than a kilometre away.

teile.einleitung: Bumblebees are large, furry wild bees that fly cheerfully buzzing from flower to flower. They are among the most important pollinators of flowers and crop plants. A bumblebee colony lives for only one summer, and it all begins with a single queen.
wichtigste: Bumblebees are wild bees and, like all insects, have six legs.
Their body is covered with a soft, fluffy fur.
In spring the queen looks for a place for a new nest, often in an old mouse hole.
The queen lays all the eggs, and the larvae are fed with pollen and nectar.
A bumblebee colony lives for only one summer, and only young queens survive the winter.
A bumblebee queen lives to be about a year old.
Bumblebees make only a little honey for their own needs.
In Switzerland there are around 40 species of bumblebee.

abschnitte.text: Bumblebees belong to the **true bees** and are related to the honeybees. They are plump and densely haired, and their fur feels soft and fluffy. Many species carry black, yellow, white or reddish-brown stripes. Like all insects they have six legs, two antennae and four wings. On the hind legs they collect flower pollen in small baskets, the so-called **pollen baskets**, called “breeches” in German.

Bumblebees drink **nectar** and collect **pollen**. They especially like to visit clover, lavender, dead-nettles, fruit trees and many other flowers. In doing so they carry pollen from flower to flower and so pollinate the plants. Some flowers, such as tomatoes, they shake out by quickly vibrating their flight muscles. That is why bumblebees are even used in greenhouses.

In spring the queen wakes from hibernation and flies around as one of the first insects. First she looks for a place for a new nest, especially often an old **mouse hole** in the ground. Some species also nest in bird boxes or under moss. From wax the queen builds small cells for the eggs and a honey pot as a store. She feeds the first larvae entirely alone with pollen and nectar.

From the first eggs hatch **workers**, who now collect food and look after the nest. The queen stays in the nest and only lays eggs. Depending on the species, a colony numbers about 50 to a few hundred animals, much fewer than in honeybees. In late summer males and young queens arise, which mate. In autumn the old colony dies, and only the young queens spend the winter in the ground.

Bumblebees can make their flight muscles shiver without moving their wings and so **warm up**. Thanks to their fur they also fly in cool weather and in the mountains. That is why you find many species of bumblebee in the Alps right up to high altitudes. If you find a tired bumblebee on the ground, you can give it a little sugar water so that it gets its strength back.

Bumblebees are very peaceful and hardly ever sting, and their sting has no barb. Many species are **endangered** today, because flowering meadows and nesting places are lacking. Pesticides also harm them. You can help with native flowers in the garden, wild corners and less lawn mowing. About 40 species of bumblebee occur in Switzerland, for example the buff-tailed bumblebee and the common carder bee.

begriffe.erklaerung: When pollen gets from one flower to another so that seeds and fruit form.
Fine flower dust that bees and bumblebees collect as protein food.
The only female in the colony that lays eggs.
A female bumblebee that collects food and looks after the nest but does not lay eggs.

gewusst: Bumblebees often fly already at temperatures at which honeybees still stay in the hive.
Bumblebees can smell whether a flower was emptied shortly before by another bumblebee.
Male bumblebees have no sting at all.

teile.einleitung: Cold-water fish are fish that are most comfortable in cool water rich in oxygen. They include many fish of our Alpine lakes and mountain streams, such as trout, char, grayling and whitefish. Because the water is getting warmer as the climate changes, they are coming under growing pressure.
wichtigste: Cold-water fish need cool water, usually below about 20 degrees.
Cold water contains more oxygen than warm water.
Trout, char, grayling, salmon and whitefish are typical cold-water fish.
Whitefish are most comfortable in cool water and live in deep lakes.
If the water is too warm, cold-water fish become stressed and can die.
The opposite are warm-water fish such as carp or catfish.

abschnitte.text: Fish are **cold-blooded**, which means their body temperature adapts to the water. Each species has a temperature range in which it lives well. **Cold-water fish** prefer cool waters, often between about 4 and 16 degrees. If it stays warmer than about 20 to 25 degrees, it becomes dangerous for many of them.

Cold water can take up more **oxygen** than warm water. Cold-water fish depend on this high oxygen content. When the water warms up, the oxygen falls, while the fish need more of it at the same time. That is why they suffer especially in summer, when streams carry little water and heat up.

The **brown trout** lives in clear, fast-flowing streams high up into the mountains. The **Arctic char** and the whitefish live in the cool depths of large lakes such as Lake Lucerne, Lake Constance or Lake Biel. Whitefish are among the most important food fish for Swiss professional fishers. The grayling and the salmon, which used to migrate up the Rhine as far as Basel and beyond, are also cold-water fish.

In hot summers the water in rivers and lakes gets warmer and warmer. In the heatwave summer of 2018 many grayling died in the **Rhine** near Schaffhausen because the water became too warm. Experts then cooled places where the fish could take refuge with cold water from streams. With climate change, cold-water fish could disappear from lower-lying waters and withdraw to higher, cooler regions.

In fishkeeping too, people speak of cold-water fish. This means fish that do not need a heater in the aquarium and live at room temperature. A well-known example is the **goldfish**, which originally comes from China. Tropical ornamental fish such as guppies, on the other hand, need a heated aquarium.

begriffe.erklaerung: An animal’s body temperature depends on its surroundings.
How much oxygen is dissolved in the water.
Silvery fish from the salmon family that live in cool lakes.
A fish that prefers warmer water, for example the carp.

gewusst: A trout can suffocate in water that is too warm, even though it is swimming right in the water.
In Switzerland many lakes have their own species of whitefish that occur only in that one lake.

teile.einleitung: Honeydew is a sticky, sugary liquid that aphids and other plant-sucking insects excrete. It is the raw material for forest honey, because bees eagerly collect it from leaves and needles. Anyone who parks their car under a lime tree in summer knows the sticky drops.
wichtigste: Honeydew is the sugary excretion of aphids.
Scale insects, cicadas and psyllids also give off honeydew.
Plant sap contains a lot of sugar but little protein.
The lice excrete the surplus sugar as honeydew.
Bees collect honeydew and make forest honey from it.
Black sooty moulds sometimes grow on honeydew.
Ants love honeydew and in return protect the aphids.

abschnitte.text: **Honeydew** is a sweet, sticky liquid that glistens on leaves, needles and twigs. It does not come from the plant itself but from small insects. Above all **aphids**, scale insects, bark aphids and cicadas excrete it. Like morning dew, it often lies in fine drops on the leaves, hence the name.

Aphids pierce the plant's vessels with their proboscis and suck the **phloem sap**. This sap contains a lot of sugar but only very little protein. To get enough protein, the lice have to take in huge amounts of it. The surplus sugar they excrete again as drops from the rear of the abdomen.

When there are few flowers, honeybees eagerly collect honeydew from spruces, firs, oaks and lime trees. From it comes **forest honey**, which tastes darker and stronger than blossom honey. It contains more minerals and often stays liquid for a long time. A well-known forest honey is fir honey, which in Switzerland is obtained, for example, in the Jura and the Pre-Alps.

In summer, honeydew drips from lime and maple trees onto cars, bicycles and garden furniture. The drops are sticky and hard to wash off. On the honeydew, **sooty moulds** often grow, which form a black coating on leaves. This coating harms plants, because it takes light away from them.

Besides bees, ants, wasps, flies and butterflies also love the sweet juice. Ants visit the aphids regularly and protect them from enemies such as ladybirds. Some researchers suspect that the biblical manna in the desert was honeydew from scale insects that became solid in the air. For beekeepers it is important to watch whether many lice sit on the forest trees, because the forest honey harvest depends on it.

begriffe.erklaerung: Sweet excretion of aphids and other plant-sucking insects.
Sugary sap that flows in the vessels of a plant.
Dark honey that bees make from honeydew.
A fungus that grows on honeydew and forms black coatings.

gewusst: Forest honey is in fact a honey that first passed through the body of aphids.
In some years there is so much honeydew that bees bring in a great deal of forest honey, and in other years almost none.
The drops under lime trees in summer are not tree resin but honeydew.

teile.einleitung: Hemimetabolism is a technical term for the incomplete metamorphosis of insects. In it, an insect develops without a pupal stage: a larva hatches from the egg that already looks like the adult animal. Grasshoppers, dragonflies and true bugs grow up in this way.
wichtigste: Hemimetabolism means incomplete metamorphosis.
The development takes place without a pupal stage.
The stages are egg, larva and adult insect.
The larvae already look like the adult animal, but do not yet have finished wings.
With every moult the larvae get bigger.
Examples are grasshoppers, crickets, true bugs, dragonflies and cockroaches.
The opposite is complete metamorphosis with a pupa, holometabolism.

abschnitte.text: The word **hemimetabolism** comes from Greek. “Hemi” means half and “metabolism” means change. So what is meant is a half or incomplete metamorphosis. In contrast to complete metamorphosis, the pupal stage is missing. Insects with this kind of development are called hemimetabolous insects.

First the female lays eggs. From the egg hatches a **larva**, which is often also called a nymph. It already looks like the adult animal, but is smaller and has only small **wing buds**. With every moult the larva grows and the wing stubs get bigger. After the last moult the insect is adult, and it is then called an **imago**.

Typical examples are grasshoppers and crickets, whose larvae look like small grasshoppers without wings. True bugs, cicadas, cockroaches, earwigs and the praying mantis also develop in this way. In **dragonflies**, the larvae live in water and look different from the adults, yet there is no pupa. Depending on the species, dragonfly larvae live in the water for several months to a few years. In the end they climb up a stalk and hatch from the last larval skin.

In **holometabolism**, complete metamorphosis, there is an additional pupal stage. Butterflies, beetles, bees and flies develop in this way. Their larvae, such as caterpillars or maggots, look quite different from the adults. In the pupa the whole body is rebuilt. In hemimetabolous insects, by contrast, the change happens step by step with every moult.

The kind of development helps researchers to classify insects and to understand how they are related. Incomplete metamorphosis is regarded as the older form of development. For larva and adult, it often means that both live in the same place and eat the same thing. In grasshoppers, for example, larvae and adults eat the same plants. If you watch insects in the garden, you can in this way tell which larva belongs to which animal.

begriffe.erklaerung: The young stage of an insect after hatching from the egg.
The adult, fully developed insect.
Complete metamorphosis with egg, larva, pupa and adult animal.
A small wing stub in larvae from which the wing later develops.

gewusst: Mayflies are the only insects that moult once more after they already have wings.
Some cicadas in North America live as larvae in the ground for 17 years before they come out.
Silverfish have no real metamorphosis at all, and look like the adults from the start.

teile.einleitung: The domestic pig is a clever and curious farm animal that descends from the wild boar. Humans have kept it for about 9,000 years, mainly for its meat. Pigs are regarded as one of the cleverest domestic animals of all.
wichtigste: The domestic pig descends from the wild boar.
A female pig is called a sow, a male a boar and the young a piglet.
A sow usually has about 8 to 12 piglets at once.
Pigs have hardly any sweat glands and cool themselves in mud.
Their sense of smell is much better than ours.
Pigs eat almost everything, plants and animals.
Researchers distinguish over twenty different grunts.

abschnitte.text: The domestic pig was bred about 9,000 years ago from the **wild boar**, both in the Middle East and in China. Domestic pigs usually have pink or spotted skin with strong, stiff **bristles**. A fully grown domestic pig can weigh well over 200 kilograms. At the front end of the snout sits the **snout** with its flat snout disc. The small curly tail is typical of many breeds of domestic pig.

The sense of smell of a pig is very good, much better than ours. With its snout it feels and smells very precisely and roots in the ground for food. That is why in France and Italy pigs have traditionally been used to search for **truffles**. Pigs are regarded as one of the cleverest domestic animals and learn quickly, for example simple tasks or their name. Researchers can distinguish over twenty different grunts.

Pigs have hardly any **sweat glands** and therefore cannot sweat like humans. So that they do not overheat in the heat, they wallow in mud, which is called **wallowing**. The layer of mud cools and protects the sensitive skin. In strong sun without mud or shade, a pig can even get sunburn. Contrary to the prejudice, pigs are in fact very clean animals and keep their sleeping area and their dung area apart.

A sow is pregnant for about three months, three weeks and three days. Before the birth she builds, if she can, a soft nest of straw. Usually about 8 to 12 **piglets** are born at once. Each piglet soon picks its own teat, at which it always drinks. When a pig is frightened, it squeals loudly and runs away.

Over a million domestic pigs live in Switzerland. In the past, pigs were often kept near cheese dairies and fed with **whey**, the liquid left over from cheesemaking. Compared with many countries, Switzerland has strict animal welfare rules, for example castrating piglets without anaesthetic has been banned since 2010. Many farms give the pigs outdoor access and straw for rooting. Pork is one of the most eaten kinds of meat in Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: A young pig.
A male pig.
Rolling in mud, with which pigs cool down and protect their skin.
An animal that eats plant and animal food.

gewusst: Pigs can work out in a mirror where food is hidden.
The snout disc of a pig is as sensitive as our fingertips.
A pig can run astonishingly fast in danger.

teile.einleitung: Hip dysplasia is a malformation of the hip joint. It occurs especially in large breeds of dog and is often inherited. For affected dogs it can mean pain when walking, but with good care many can still lead a good life.
wichtigste: Hip dysplasia is a malformation of the hip joint.
The hip socket is too shallow, so the head of the thigh bone does not sit properly in it.
The disease is common in some breeds of dog and is inherited.
Large breeds such as the German Shepherd, Labrador or Bernese Mountain Dog are especially often affected.
Growing too fast and being overweight can make the disease worse.
Vets usually recognise hip dysplasia on an X-ray.
Humans too, especially babies, can have hip dysplasia.

abschnitte.text: The hip joint is a **ball-and-socket joint**. The round head of the thigh bone sits in a hollow of the pelvis, the **hip socket**. In hip dysplasia this socket is too shallow or the head has the wrong shape. As a result the joint sits too loosely and wobbles with every movement. With time, cartilage and bone wear down.

Hip dysplasia is among the most common **hereditary diseases** in dogs. Above all large and heavy breeds are affected, such as the German Shepherd, the Labrador Retriever, the Golden Retriever, the Rottweiler and the Bernese Mountain Dog. Small dogs have the disease much more rarely. It also occurs in cats, for example in the large breed Maine Coon.

The most important cause is the **genes** that a puppy inherits from its parents. But the environment also plays a part. If a young dog grows too fast, gets too much food or becomes too fat, this puts great strain on the hip. Too wild stair-climbing and jumping in puppyhood can also do harm. That is why puppies of large breeds should grow slowly and evenly.

Affected dogs often get up with difficulty or do not like stairs. Some walk unsteadily or hop with both hind legs at the same time like a hare. The vet takes an **X-ray** of the hip, usually under a light anaesthetic. In Europe the result is graded in steps from A (free) to E (severe). Many breeding clubs, in Switzerland too, allow only dogs with good hips to be bred from.

The malformation cannot be cured, but a lot can be done about it. Important are a slim body weight and regular, gentle exercise such as swimming. **Physiotherapy** strengthens the muscles that support the joint. Against pain the vet gives medicines. In severe cases an artificial hip joint can be fitted, similar to humans.

Humans too can be born with hip dysplasia. In babies the hip is therefore examined with **ultrasound** in the first weeks of life. If the malformation is discovered early, it can often be treated well with abduction pants or a splint. The legs are held slightly spread so that the socket can grow properly.

begriffe.erklaerung: The joint that connects the thigh with the pelvis.
A disease that is passed on from parents to children.
Wear of cartilage and bone in a joint that causes pain.
A picture that shows the bones in the body with invisible rays.

gewusst: Because dogs with hip dysplasia often move the hind legs together, their gait is sometimes called “Hasenhoppeln” in German, literally “hare hopping”.
At one year old you can usually see reliably on the X-ray whether a dog has healthy hips.
Swimming is ideal for dogs with hip dysplasia, because the water bears the weight.

teile.einleitung: The goldfish is one of the best-known ornamental fish in the world. It swims in aquariums, garden ponds and park fountains and usually glows orange or golden. Its ancestor was an inconspicuous grey fish from China.
wichtigste: The goldfish belongs to the carp family.
It has its name from its often golden-orange colour.
People have kept goldfish as ornamental animals for over a thousand years.
Goldfish eat both plants and small animals.
In one spawning, a female lays several hundred to a thousand eggs.
Goldfish have no eyelids and cannot close their eyes.
A goldfish needs a large enough aquarium or a pond.

abschnitte.text: The goldfish has the scientific name **Carassius auratus** and belongs to the **carp family**. Most goldfish are orange, golden, red, white or spotted. Young goldfish are often bronze at first and get their bright colour only later. In a large pond a goldfish can grow to over 20 centimetres long. It has no eyelids, so it can never close its eyes, not even when resting.

The goldfish descends from a wild Prussian carp that lives in East Asia and looks rather grey-green. In **China**, over a thousand years ago, people noticed individual red-golden fish and began to keep and breed them deliberately. Later goldfish came to Japan and, from the 17th century, to Europe too. Through **breeding**, many forms arose, such as the veiltail with its long fins or the celestial eye, whose eyes look upwards.

Goldfish are omnivores and eat plant parts, algae, insect larvae, small crustaceans and worms. At feeding time they often swim excitedly to the surface of the water, because they have learned that something is coming then. Anyone who gives too much food harms the fish, because leftover food spoils and makes the **water** dirty. The fish can then fall ill. It is better to feed only as much as the fish eat up in a few minutes.

In spring, when the water gets warmer, the **spawning season** begins. The males then often get small white dots on the gill covers and pectoral fins, which are called **spawning tubercles**. They chase the females through the water until these lay several hundred to a thousand sticky eggs on water plants. After a few days, tiny larvae hatch. Adult goldfish sometimes eat their freshly hatched young, so only a few survive in a pond.

abschnitte.titel: Keeping in an aquarium and a pond
abschnitte.text: A goldfish needs a lot of space, clean water and others of its kind, because it likes to live in a group. Small ball-shaped **goldfish bowls** are unsuitable for the animals and count as cruelty to animals. In a garden pond, goldfish can spend the winter outdoors if the water is deep enough. It is important that the pond does not freeze over completely in winter, so that enough **oxygen** gets into the water. Well cared for, goldfish can live to over 20 years old.

In many Swiss gardens and parks there are ponds with goldfish. But you must never release goldfish into streams or lakes. There they multiply strongly, eat the spawn and larvae of frogs and newts and displace native animals. Such introduced species are called **invasive species**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large family of fish that includes carp, goldfish and many other freshwater fish.
What it is called when fish lay their eggs in the water.
Humans select animals with certain features and let them reproduce.
An animal or plant species that was introduced by humans and displaces native species.

gewusst: Goldfish can remember things for weeks and months, and the rumour of a three-second memory is not true.
Released goldfish can lose their colour in the wild and turn greyish again like their wild ancestors.
The goldfish was one of the first fish that humans bred purely as pets.

teile.einleitung: The domestic rabbit is a popular pet and descends from the European wild rabbit. Rabbits are sociable animals that need a lot of space, company and the right food. With good care they can live to be about 8 to 12 years old.
wichtigste: All domestic rabbits descend from the European wild rabbit.
Rabbits belong to the lagomorphs and not to the rodents.
They are social animals and should never live alone.
They need enough space for hopping and hiding.
Their main food is hay, with fresh greens and vegetables added.
Their teeth keep growing throughout life.
Domestic rabbits live to be about 8 to 12 years old.

abschnitte.text: All domestic rabbits descend from the **European wild rabbit**, which originally lived on the Iberian Peninsula. The Romans already kept rabbits in enclosures. In the Middle Ages they were bred mainly in monasteries in France and gradually became **pets**. Today there are dozens of breeds, from the dwarf rabbit to the giant rabbit.

Rabbits have long ears, soft fur and strong hind legs for hopping. Popular are **dwarf rabbits**, which weigh only about one to two kilograms. **Lop-eared rabbits** have drooping ears, and giant rabbits can weigh over six kilograms. They come in many colours, from white through grey to spotted.

Rabbits are **social animals** and need at least one other of their kind, and a guinea pig does not replace this. They need a lot of space for hopping, running and zigzagging, as well as little houses for **hiding**. A run outdoors or a large enclosure is better than a small cage. In Switzerland, animal welfare law requires that animals that live socially must have contact with others of their kind.

The most important food for rabbits is **hay**, which should always be available. Added to this are grass, herbs, leafy greens and some vegetables such as carrots. Because their **teeth** keep growing, they have to chew a lot so that the teeth wear down. Sweets, bread and too much dry food make rabbits ill.

A doe carries her young for about 31 days, and then usually four to eight young are born. Young rabbits are **altricial**: they are naked and blind and stay in the nest at first. When a rabbit feels content, it sometimes makes leaps of joy into the air. In danger it thumps loudly on the ground with its hind legs to warn the others.

begriffe.erklaerung: An order of mammals that includes hares, rabbits and pikas.
A young animal that is helpless at birth and stays in the nest for a long time.
What a female rabbit is called.
What a male rabbit is called.

gewusst: Rabbits eat part of their droppings again to get all the nutrients out of their food.
A rabbit can turn its ears independently of each other.
In rabbit show jumping, called Kaninhop, rabbits on a lead jump over small obstacles, similar to horses in show jumping.

teile.einleitung: “Heidi” is a famous children's novel by the Swiss writer Johanna Spyri. It tells of an orphan girl who lives with her grandfather on an Alp in Graubünden and tends the goats with Goat-Peter. Heidi is one of the best-known Swiss stories in the world.
wichtigste: “Heidi” was written by the Zurich writer Johanna Spyri.
The story appeared in two parts, in 1880 and 1881.
Heidi lives with the Alp-Uncle on an Alp above Maienfeld in Graubünden.
With Goat-Peter, Heidi tends the goats in the mountains.
In Frankfurt, Heidi becomes friends with Klara, who uses a wheelchair.
The book has been translated into many languages and filmed often.
A Japanese cartoon series made Heidi known worldwide from 1974.

abschnitte.text: The novel was written by **Johanna Spyri**, who was born in 1827 in Hirzel in the canton of Zurich and died in 1901. The first part is called “Heidi's Years of Learning and Travel” and appeared in 1880. The second part, “Heidi Makes Use of What She Has Learned”, followed in 1881. The books quickly became a great success. Today they are among the most widely read books from Switzerland.

The orphan **Heidi** is brought by her Aunt Dete to her grandfather, the grumpy **Alp-Uncle**. He lives alone in a hut high above the village. Heidi wins his heart with her cheerful nature and loves life in the mountains. Later she has to go to Frankfurt to the rich Sesemann family, where she is to be a companion to the disabled Klara. There Heidi becomes terribly homesick, until at last she is allowed to return to the Alp.

The **goats** play an important part in the novel. Goat-Peter drives the goats of the village out to pasture every morning, and Heidi goes along. The grandfather's goats are called Schwänli and Bärli. Their fresh milk and life in the mountain air make the children strong and healthy. When Klara comes to visit later, she learns to walk again on the Alp.

Heidi has been filmed many times, for example in 1952 in Switzerland and in 2015 with Bruno Ganz as the Alp-Uncle. Especially famous is the Japanese **cartoon series** of 1974, on which the later animation master Hayao Miyazaki also worked. Through this series many people in Japan and Europe know Switzerland above all as the land of Heidi. There are also musicals, radio plays and new animated series. In this way Heidi has accompanied generations of children.

The story is set in the area around **Maienfeld** in the canton of Graubünden. Today there is a Heidi village there with a Heidi house, which many tourists from all over the world visit. The whole holiday region around Maienfeld and Bad Ragaz calls itself **Heidiland**. Heidi has become a symbol of the Swiss Alps, Alpine farming and nature. Many people think first of mountains, goats and Heidi when they think of Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mountain pasture where animals graze in summer.
Heidi's grandfather, who lives alone on the Alp (“Alpöhi” in German).
The goatherd and Heidi's best friend (“Geissenpeter” in German).
A sad feeling when you long for your home.

gewusst: “Heidi” has been translated into a great many languages and is among the best-known children's books in the world.
In Frankfurt, Heidi sleepwalks through the house out of sheer homesickness, and at first everyone thinks it is haunted.
Many people in Japan travel to Maienfeld specially because of the cartoon series.

teile.einleitung: A honey extractor is a device with which beekeepers take the honey out of the honeycombs. The combs are spun quickly in it, so that the honey is flung out. The great thing about it is that the combs stay whole and can be given back to the bees.
wichtigste: With the honey extractor, the beekeeper takes honey out of the combs.
It works by spinning quickly and by centrifugal force.
Before extracting, the wax caps of the combs are removed.
The combs stay whole in the process and can be reused.
The honey extractor was invented in 1865 by Franz Hruschka.
After extracting, the honey is sieved and filled into jars.

abschnitte.text: The **honey extractor** is a large container made of stainless steel, with a rotating basket inside. The beekeeper places the comb frames from the beehive in this basket. Small extractors are turned by hand with a crank, larger ones with an electric motor. Almost every beekeeper in Switzerland owns one or shares one with others.

When the basket spins quickly, **centrifugal force** acts on the honey. It presses the honey out of the open cells against the wall of the container. From there it flows downwards and collects at the bottom. Through a tap, the beekeeper then lets the honey run into a bucket.

First the beekeeper takes the full honey combs out of the hive, whose cells are sealed with wax. With an **uncapping fork** he removes the thin wax caps. Then the combs are spun and the honey is poured through a sieve that holds back little bits of wax and bee parts. After a few days of rest it is filled into jars.

The honey extractor was invented in 1865 by the Austrian officer and beekeeper **Franz Hruschka**. Before that, the combs mostly had to be crushed and pressed to get at the honey. In the process the combs were destroyed, and the bees had to build everything anew. The extractor made beekeeping much easier and more productive.

To build wax, bees need a great deal of energy and food. Because the combs stay whole when extracted, the beekeeper can give them back to the bees. In this way the bees can fill them with honey again straight away. Since the beekeeper takes honey away from the bees, he feeds them sugar water in late summer as **winter feed**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A force that pushes everything outwards when spinning quickly.
Removing the wax caps from the honey cells.
A wooden frame in which the bees build their comb.
Sugar solution that the beekeeper gives the bees as a replacement for the harvested honey.

gewusst: The honey extractor works on the same principle as the spin cycle in a washing machine.
Very thick heather honey can hardly be extracted and has to be loosened beforehand.
Because the combs stay whole, the bees save a lot of work building wax.

t1ly4uyk.t: The bond between dogs and humans

teile.einleitung: Dogs and humans have lived together for many thousands of years, longer than with any other animal. In that time, dogs have learned to understand us humans astonishingly well. Researchers today study closely how this special friendship works.
wichtigste: The dog is the oldest domestic animal of humans.
Dogs can recognise human facial expressions and react to them.
Dogs much more often actively seek eye contact with humans than wolves do.
Dogs understand pointing gestures, for example when you point at a hiding place.
When dog and human look at each other, the bonding hormone oxytocin rises in both.
Dogs work as helpers, for example as guide dogs for the blind or rescue dogs.
A good relationship is based on trust, patience and clear rules.

abschnitte.text: Even in the Stone Age, dogs lived together with humans. In **Bonn-Oberkassel** in Germany, a grave was found that is about 14,000 years old and in which humans were buried together with a dog. Dogs helped with hunting, guarded camps and kept people warm at night. In return, humans gave them food and protection. In this way a partnership arose from which both benefited.

Studies show that dogs recognise human **facial expressions**. They distinguish a cheerful face from an angry one and react to it. They also hear from the voice whether we are friendly or strict. When you point at a cup under which there is food, a dog often follows the **pointing gesture**. Even chimpanzees find this task harder.

Researchers have compared dogs and tame wolves with each other. Dogs much more often actively seek **eye contact** with humans. In an unsolvable task, dogs look at their humans as if asking for help. Wolves, by contrast, tend to keep trying alone. Dogs also have a special muscle above the eye with which they can make the well-known **puppy-dog eyes**.

When dog and human look at each other lovingly or stroke, the hormone **oxytocin** rises in both. It is also called the bonding hormone, because it promotes trust and closeness. The same hormone also plays an important part between parents and babies. Many people feel less alone with a dog and move more.

Dogs take on many tasks for humans. **Guide dogs for the blind** lead visually impaired people safely through traffic. Avalanche dogs and rescue dogs search for buried people, in Switzerland for example through the organisation REDOG. Sniffer dogs find drugs or explosives, and **therapy dogs** visit the sick and elderly. Herding dogs help farmers with driving sheep.

A dog needs trust, clear rules and a lot of patience. It learns best with praise and reward instead of punishment. Children should never stroke a strange dog without the owner's permission. You do not disturb a dog while it is eating or sleeping. Anyone who understands the dog's **body language** recognises in good time when it wants to be left in peace.

begriffe.erklaerung: A hormone in the body that promotes trust and affection.
When two living things look into each other's eyes.
A movement with arm or finger that points to something.
How an animal or human communicates something with posture, expression and movements.

gewusst: Dogs sometimes yawn along when a familiar person yawns.
Many dogs know dozens of words, and individual especially gifted dogs even know the names of over a hundred toys.
Even puppies that have had hardly any contact with humans understand simple pointing gestures.

teile.einleitung: In German, “gründeln” is the word used when an animal looks for food on the bottom of a body of water. Carp root about in the mud with their mouths, and ducks dip their heads under and stick their rear ends up in the air. Once you have seen it, you recognise it at once.
wichtigste: Gründeln means looking for food on the bottom of a body of water.
Carp feed on the bottom by sucking in mud and sieving out food.
You recognise fish that are feeding on the bottom by the stirred-up, cloudy water.
Ducks also feed like this, sticking their rear ends out of the water.
Ducks that feed like this are called dabbling ducks, for example the mallard.
Fish that feed on the bottom can cloud a body of water badly.

abschnitte.text: The German word **gründeln** comes from “Grund”, the bottom of a lake, pond or river. It means searching for food on the bed of a body of water. Many small animals live there, such as mosquito larvae, worms, snails and mussels. In addition, plant remains and seeds sink to the bottom. Fish and waterbirds have developed quite different techniques for getting at this food.

abschnitte.titel: Fish that feed on the bottom
abschnitte.text: Typical bottom-feeding fish are **carp**, tench, bream and barbel. The carp has a mouth that it can push forward like a snout, and four **barbels** on its upper lip. With the barbels it feels and tastes in the mud. It sucks in mud, keeps the lumps of food and pushes the rest out again through the gills. This leaves small craters in the bottom and rising air bubbles.

When a carp feeds on the bottom, it stirs up a lot of mud, so you can often recognise it by the **cloudy water**. Anglers look out for such clouding and bubbles to find carp. If very many carp live in a small pond, the water stays permanently cloudy. Then water plants get less light and grow worse. That is why conservationists make sure that not too many carp live in small ponds.

Many ducks also feed on the bottom, and they are called **dabbling ducks**. They include the mallard, the teal, the gadwall and the shoveler. They do not dive right under, but tip forward, put their head and neck into the water and stick their rear end vertically up in the air. This lets them reach plants and small animals in shallow water. Swans also feed like this, and with their long neck they reach particularly deep.

On almost every Swiss lake or pond you can watch mallards feeding on the bottom, especially well on shallow stretches of shore. By contrast, **diving ducks** such as the tufted duck dive right under and swim down to the bottom. Carp live in many warm lakes and ponds of the Central Plateau. On quiet summer days you sometimes see the water at the shore suddenly turn cloudy when a carp is feeding there.

begriffe.erklaerung: Thread-like growths on the mouth of some fish with which they feel and taste.
A duck that puts only its head and neck under water to feed.
A duck that dives right under to look for food on the bottom.

begriffe.wort: Bed of a body of water
begriffe.erklaerung: The bottom of a lake, pond or river.

gewusst: The small fish called the gudgeon, in German Gründling, also has its name from feeding on the bottom.
A dabbling duck looks from a distance like a small shuttlecock sticking out of the water.
Dabbling ducks can feed only in shallow water, because they have to reach the bottom with their heads.

teile.einleitung: Cockatoos are parrots with a striking crest of feathers that they can raise when they are excited. They live in Australia and on the islands to the north of it. Cockatoos are very intelligent and loud, and they can live to a great age.
wichtigste: Cockatoos form the bird family Cacatuidae, with around 21 species.
All cockatoos have a crest of feathers that they can raise.
There are no blue or green cockatoos, because their feathers lack the Dyck structure.
About half of all species are found only in Australia.
The cockatiel is the smallest kind of cockatoo.
The word cockatoo comes from the Malay language.
Like all parrots, they have two toes pointing forwards and two pointing backwards.

abschnitte.text: A typical feature of **cockatoos** is the movable **crest** on the head, which they raise like a fan when they are excited. Their plumage is mostly white, pink, grey or black. There are no blue or green cockatoos, because their feathers lack the **Dyck structure**, a fine layer that produces blue in other parrots. They have a strong, curved beak that can crack even hard nuts.

The cockatoo family includes around 21 species. They live in Australia, New Guinea, Indonesia, the Philippines and the Solomon Islands, but they do not occur naturally on Borneo. About half of all species live only in **Australia**. Well-known species are the sulphur-crested cockatoo, the pink and grey galah and the large black palm cockatoo.

Cockatoos eat seeds, nuts, fruit, tubers, roots and sometimes insect larvae. Their feet have two toes pointing forwards and two backwards, so they can grip food as if with a hand. Special **powder down** feathers crumble into a fine powder that cares for the plumage and makes it water-repellent. Anyone who strokes a cockatoo often ends up with white dust on their fingers.

Cockatoos usually live in flocks and call loudly and shrilly. They are very **intelligent**, solve puzzles and sometimes use tools. The palm cockatoo even drums on a tree with a stick to impress a female. They nest in tree hollows, and both parents look after the young.

The **cockatiel** is the smallest kind of cockatoo and is placed in a subfamily of its own, the Nymphicinae. Its genus name Nymphicus refers to the nymphs of mythology. It comes from Australia and is a popular pet here. It too has a crest and orange patches on its cheeks.

Many cockatoos are kept as pets, but they need plenty of space, things to do and company of their own kind. In captivity some species can live to more than 60 years old, and a Major Mitchell’s cockatoo in a zoo near Chicago even reached the age of 83. Some species are seriously threatened by loss of habitat and illegal capture. In Australian cities, on the other hand, some cockatoos are a common sight in parks.

begriffe.erklaerung: Long feathers on the head that can be raised.
Special feathers that crumble into a fine powder and care for the plumage.
A layer in feathers that scatters light so that they look blue.
A group of birds that live and fly together.

gewusst: Sulphur-crested cockatoos in Sydney have learned to open wheelie bin lids, and other cockatoos copy the trick.
The palm cockatoo is one of the few birds that drum a rhythm using a tool.

teile.einleitung: A herd animal is an animal that by nature lives in a group with others of its kind. Sheep, cattle, horses and goats are typical herd animals. Alone, they feel unsure and stressed.
wichtigste: A herd animal is an animal that lives in a group.
A large group of sheep is called a flock.
Sheep like best to stay in the group, because they feel safer that way.
When sheep are frightened, they quickly run away close together.
Many herd animals are plant-eaters and flight animals.
In Switzerland, many herd animals may not be kept alone.
Herd animals communicate with sounds, smells and body language.

abschnitte.text: A **herd animal** does not live alone but together with many others of its kind. Typical herd animals are sheep, cattle, goats, horses, zebras, wildebeest and elephants. Most of them are plant-eaters that live on open meadows or in steppes. There are few hiding places there, so the group is their most important protection. Humans, too, keep most of their farm animals in herds.

Herd animals are mostly **flight animals**, which in danger prefer to run away rather than fight. Sheep like best to stay together, because they feel safer in the group. When they are frightened, they quickly run away close together. The closer the animals are to each other, the harder it is for a wolf to attack a single animal. Many eyes and ears also notice dangers sooner.

In the herd there is a **ranking order** that avoids quarrels. The animals communicate with sounds, smells and **body language**, for example with the position of the ears or the carriage of the head. Often the others follow an experienced lead animal. Herd animals do many things at the same time: they eat, rest and wander together. Mothers and young recognise each other even in large groups by voice and smell.

Because herd animals need company, they suffer when they have to live alone. Swiss **animal welfare law** therefore requires that, for example, horses, sheep and goats have contact with others of their kind. A horse should at least be able to see, hear and smell other horses. Anyone who keeps herd animals therefore always needs at least two animals. Enough space and outdoor access are also important, so that weaker animals can get out of the way.

Humans, too, sometimes behave like herd animals and copy what many others do. This is called **herd instinct** or herd behaviour. One example is when everyone goes into a restaurant just because many people are already sitting there. Sometimes this is useful, and sometimes it leads to wrong decisions. It is therefore worth thinking for yourself instead of simply following the crowd.

begriffe.erklaerung: An animal that by nature lives in a group.
An animal that in danger prefers to flee rather than fight.
Animals of the same species.
The need to behave like the group.

gewusst: A sheep that is separated from its flock often bleats loudly and desperately tries to get back.
Sheep can remember the faces of many others of their kind for a long time.
In zebras, the many stripes in the herd confuse predators, because they find it hard to pick out single animals.

teile.einleitung: The Greyhound is a slim sighthound from Great Britain and the fastest breed of dog in the world. On racetracks it reaches speeds of around 70 kilometres per hour. At home, by contrast, it is often calm, gentle and likes to sleep a lot.
wichtigste: The Greyhound is the fastest breed of dog in the world.
It can run at about 70 kilometres per hour.
Greyhounds belong to the sighthounds, which hunt mainly with their eyes.
The breed comes from Great Britain and Ireland.
Greyhounds are often used for dog racing.
In the house they are usually calm and friendly family dogs.
Many former racing dogs look for a new home after their career.

abschnitte.text: The Greyhound is a large, very slim dog with a shoulder height of about 68 to 76 centimetres. It has a long, narrow head, a deep chest and a narrow **waist**. Its coat is short and smooth and comes in many colours, such as black, white, reddish brown or brindle. The long legs and the flexible back make it a perfect runner. Under the thin coat you can often see its strong muscles.

At around 70 kilometres per hour, the Greyhound is the fastest dog. When running, it stretches and bends its back like a spring and touches the ground only briefly with each bound. It has a large heart and strong lungs. But it is a **sprinter**: it keeps up very high speeds only over short distances. Only a few animals such as the cheetah or the pronghorn are faster on land.

Greyhounds belong to the **sighthounds**, which pursue their prey mainly with their eyes and not with their nose. Such dogs were bred as long ago as antiquity for hunting hares. In England, for a long time only nobles were allowed to keep Greyhounds. Today hunting with dogs by coursing is banned in Switzerland and many other countries.

In **greyhound racing**, the dogs chase an artificial hare that is pulled along a rail over the track. Especially in Great Britain, Ireland and Australia there are many racetracks. Critics complain that some racing dogs are badly treated or no longer needed after their career. That is why there are associations that find homes with families for former racing dogs, also in Switzerland.

Although it is so fast, the Greyhound is regarded as calm and easy-going in the house, and it often sleeps many hours a day. It is usually friendly, gentle and rather reserved. Because it has little fat and a thin coat, it gets cold quickly and often wears a **dog coat** in winter. It should only be let off the lead in fenced areas, because when it sees something moving, the urge to chase can seize it. Greyhounds live to be about 10 to 14 years old.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of slim, fast dogs that pursue their prey with their eyes.
A group of dogs with shared features that has been deliberately bred.
A runner who runs very fast over short distances.
The innate urge of an animal to pursue prey.

gewusst: A Greyhound can reach a very high speed after just a few bounds.
Greyhounds can move their eyes far to the side and so see almost all around.
A well-known American bus company has the name Greyhound and a running sighthound in its logo.

teile.einleitung: Genetic diversity means that the animals or plants of a species differ in their genetic make-up. That is why not every fox looks exactly the same and not every cow is equally resistant. These differences are like a toolbox with which a species can adapt to new conditions.
wichtigste: Genetic diversity is the variety of genetic make-up within a species.
Besides the diversity of species and of habitats, it is a part of biodiversity.
Genetic diversity increases the ability to adapt to changes in the environment.
That is why it is very important for the protection of species.
Small, isolated populations often lose genetic diversity.
Inbreeding can favour illnesses and weaknesses.
Old breeds of farm animals and plant varieties also preserve genetic diversity.

abschnitte.text: Every living thing has **genes** in its cells, which act like a blueprint. Within a species there are slightly different versions of many genes. That is why people have different eye colours, and cats have different coat patterns. The more such versions there are in a species, the greater its genetic diversity. It is one of three levels of **biodiversity**, alongside the diversity of species and of habitats.

The environment is constantly changing, for example through the climate, new diseases or new enemies. If the animals of a species are different, some may have exactly the characteristics that help in the new situation. These animals are more likely to survive and pass on their genes. In this way genetic diversity increases the **adaptability** of a species. If, on the other hand, all the animals are almost the same, a single disease can threaten a whole population.

When only a few animals of a species are left, close relatives often mate. This is called **inbreeding**. Hereditary diseases can then occur more often, and the animals sometimes become weaker or less fertile. A well-known example is the cheetah, whose genetic diversity is very low. It is suspected that its ancestors were once, long ago, reduced to very few animals.

The Alpine ibex was wiped out in Switzerland in the 19th century. From 1906, animals from Italy were reintroduced, all of which came from one small remnant population. Today many thousands of ibex live in the Swiss Alps again, but their genetic diversity is low. Experts therefore take care to connect populations with each other. The bearded vulture, too, is bred and released in such a way that as much diversity as possible is preserved.

Zoos keep **studbooks** so that related animals do not always have young together. For plants, seed banks store the seeds of many varieties, for example the large seed vault on Svalbard in Norway. In Switzerland, the foundation **ProSpecieRara** has worked since 1982 for old breeds of farm animals and plant varieties. Wildlife bridges over motorways help animals to move between areas and to mix. In this way genetic diversity is preserved in the future too.

begriffe.erklaerung: A section of the genetic material that helps to determine a particular characteristic.
The diversity of life: species, habitats and genetic make-up.
Reproduction between closely related animals.
The ability to cope with new environmental conditions.

gewusst: All the ibex in Switzerland descend from only a few dozen animals from an Italian mountain valley.
In Ireland in the 19th century, a fungal disease led to a great famine, partly because almost everywhere the same variety of potato was grown.
Cheetahs are so similar genetically that in experiments skin from an unrelated animal could be transplanted onto them without being rejected.

teile.einleitung: Rabbits are small, nimble mammals with long ears and a stubby tail. The wild rabbit is the ancestor of all domestic rabbits, which live as pets in many families today. Although they look like hares, rabbits are a species of their own with very different habits.
wichtigste: The male is called a buck, the female a doe.
Baby rabbits are born naked and blind.
Rabbits have almost all-round vision.
They are mainly active at dusk, in the morning and evening.
In danger they flee in a zigzag into their burrows.
They eat their soft night droppings again, because these contain important nutrients.
Rabbits are not rodents, but lagomorphs.

abschnitte.text: A wild rabbit weighs about 1.5 to 2.5 kilograms and has soft, thick, greyish-brown fur. Its ears are shorter than those of a hare. The eyes sit at the sides of the head, so the rabbit has almost **all-round vision** and sees enemies early. The split upper lip is called a **hare lip**, and the long whiskers help it feel its way in narrow tunnels.

Wild rabbits originally come from the **Iberian Peninsula**, that is, from Spain and Portugal. They live in groups and dig branching underground burrows with many exits. They like open countryside with loose soil, hedges and meadows. In Switzerland wild rabbits are rare; the brown hare is seen more often here.

Rabbits eat grass, herbs, leaves and, in winter, bark and twigs too. Their teeth keep growing all their lives and are worn down by chewing. Because plants are hard to digest, they eat their soft night droppings, the **caecotrophs**, a second time. In this way they extract important vitamins and proteins.

After a pregnancy of about a month, the doe gives birth in a nest padded with fur, usually to four to ten young. Baby rabbits are naked and blind: they are **altricial**. After about ten days they open their eyes, and after about three weeks they leave the nest. Because rabbits multiply so fast, they can become very numerous in a short time.

Rabbits are out and about mainly at dawn and dusk. In danger they thump the ground with their hind legs and so warn the others. Then they run away in a **zigzag** so that a fox or bird of prey has a hard time catching them. A contented rabbit lies relaxed when stroked and closes its eyes.

Domestic rabbits come in many breeds, from the dwarf rabbit to the large Continental Giant. Rabbits are sociable animals and should never be kept alone; in Switzerland the **Animal Welfare Act** also requires this. They need plenty of space to hop around, hay, fresh water and green food. Rabbits are also kept as farm animals for meat and fur.

begriffe.erklaerung: A male rabbit.
A female rabbit.
A young animal that is born helpless and stays in the nest for a long time.
Soft, nutrient-rich droppings that rabbits eat again.
A group of animals that includes hares, rabbits and pikas.

gewusst: Rabbits have two small teeth, the peg teeth, behind the large upper incisors.
In 1859 about two dozen wild rabbits were released in Australia, and they later became hundreds of millions.
A rabbit can jump into the air for joy and twist as it does so, which is called a binky.

teile.einleitung: Cold-bloods are heavy, powerful horses that were bred in the past mainly for hard work. They pulled ploughs, carts and tree trunks. The name has nothing to do with body temperature, but with their calm, relaxed nature.
wichtigste: Cold-blood is a collective term for heavy working horses.
Cold-bloods have the same warm blood as all other horses.
Their name describes their calm and patient temperament.
In the past they pulled ploughs, carriages, brewery wagons and timber.
Many weigh from 700 to over 1,000 kilograms.
Well-known breeds are the Shire horse, the Belgian, the Percheron and the Noriker.
Today they are working in forests more often again, because they are gentle on the ground.

abschnitte.text: **Cold-blood** is not a term from biology but from horse breeding. Horses are roughly divided into thoroughbreds, warm-bloods and cold-bloods, depending on build and nature. Cold-bloods are the heaviest and calmest horses. Their blood is of course just as warm as that of all horses; the name refers to their **temperament**.

Cold-bloods have a massive body, a broad back, a powerful chest and thick, strong legs. Many have long hair around the fetlocks, called **feathering**. They usually weigh between 700 and over 1,000 kilograms. The **Shire horse** from England is one of the largest horses in the world and can reach a shoulder height of over 1.80 metres.

Before there were tractors and lorries, cold-bloods were the most important helpers in farming and transport. They pulled **ploughs** and harrows, harvest wagons, stagecoaches and heavy beer barrels. In towns they pulled trams and delivery carts. With the invention of motor vehicles in the 20th century they became rare, and many breeds almost died out.

Today cold-bloods are used again for **logging with horses**, that is, for hauling tree trunks out of the forest. They protect the forest floor better than heavy machines and can also reach steep ground. They also pull carriages at festivals, weddings and for tourists. Many people ride them for leisure too, because they are calm and reliable.

Well-known cold-blood breeds are the **Belgian**, the French Percheron, the Austrian Noriker, the English Shire horse and the Black Forest horse. In Switzerland the **Franches-Montagnes horse** from the Jura is well known, the only horse breed that originally comes from Switzerland.
