At places such as Kuril Lake, many bears gather and catch fish with their paws and mouths. In this way they build up a thick layer of fat for the winter.

Outside the salmon season, Kamchatka brown bears usually live alone. In late autumn they withdraw to a den and go into **winter dormancy**, during which they eat nothing for months. In winter the female usually gives birth in the den to two or three tiny cubs. The cubs stay with their mother for about two to three years.

Kamchatka brown bears are a magnet for nature photographers and tourists from all over the world. In protected areas such as the South Kamchatka Nature Park, you can watch them fishing. They are threatened by poaching, partly because of their gall bladder, which is used in traditional medicine. Overfishing of salmon also takes away their food.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group within a species that differs slightly in appearance or range.
A long sleep in winter during which the body saves energy.
An animal that eats both plants and animals.
A piece of land that is almost completely surrounded by water.

gewusst: In the salmon season a Kamchatka brown bear can eat many kilograms of fish a day and quickly put on weight.
The Kamchatka Peninsula is about six times the size of Switzerland, but has only a very thin population.

teile.einleitung: The hornet is the largest wasp in Europe and clearly bigger than an ordinary wasp. Despite its dangerous reputation, it is rather peaceful and attacks only when its nest is threatened. As a hunter of many other insects, it is an important part of nature.
wichtigste: The hornet is the largest species of wasp in Europe.
It is clearly bigger than an ordinary wasp.
Its body is coloured reddish brown and yellow.
Hornets build their nests from chewed wood that looks like paper.
They hunt many other insects to feed their larvae.
Only the young queens survive the winter.
Hornets are more peaceful than their reputation.

abschnitte.text: The European hornet, scientifically Vespa crabro, is easy to recognise by its size. Workers grow to about two to two and a half centimetres long, the **queen** even over three centimetres. Head and thorax are coloured reddish brown, and the abdomen is yellow with brown bands. In this way it looks different from the black-and-yellow wasps that snack at our plates in summer.

Hornets like to build their nest in hollow trees, bird nest boxes, sheds or attics. The nest consists of chewed, rotting wood that looks like **paper**. In spring a queen founds the nest alone, and by late summer the colony grows to several hundred animals. In autumn the whole colony dies, and only the young, mated queens spend the winter in hiding places.

Hornets are skilful **hunters**. They catch flies, horseflies, wasps, caterpillars and other insects and feed them to their larvae. The adult hornets themselves drink mainly tree sap and the juice of windfall fruit. Unlike many wasps, they hardly take any interest in cake or sweet drinks.

Hornets are rather shy and sting only when you disturb their nest or trap them. Their venom is no stronger than that of bees or wasps. The old claim that a few hornet stings could kill a human or a horse is false. A sting is dangerous only for people with an **allergy** or when it is a sting in the mouth or throat.

The European hornet occurs throughout Switzerland at lower altitudes. It helps to keep the number of harmful insects small. Since 2017, the **Asian hornet** has been spreading in Switzerland, an introduced species with a dark body and yellow legs. It especially likes to hunt honeybees, so finds are reported to the authorities.

begriffe.erklaerung: The female that founds a colony of hornets and lays all the eggs.
A young insect that develops into the adult hornet in the nest.
An exaggerated defensive reaction of the body, for example to insect venom.
An introduced species of animal or plant that harms native species.

gewusst: Hornets also fly at night and are sometimes lured into houses by the light.
A hornet colony catches a large number of insects every day in summer.
A hornet's nest is used for only one summer and is not occupied again the next year.

teile.einleitung: A herd is a group of animals of the same species that live, feed and move on together. Herds are found above all in hoofed animals such as cows, sheep, horses or wildebeest. On Swiss farms and Alpine pastures, too, you see many herds.
wichtigste: Several cows that live together on a pasture are called a herd.
A herd animal is an animal that lives in a group.
In a herd, animals are better protected from enemies.
Many herds have a ranking order and a lead animal.
People who look after herds are called herdswomen and herdsmen.
For other animals people say, instead of herd, for example pack or shoal.
The largest herds in the world are formed by wildebeest in East Africa.

abschnitte.text: A **herd** is a group of animals of the same species that live together. Herds are usually spoken of in the case of large plant-eaters such as cattle, sheep, goats, horses, deer or elephants. The animals often eat, rest and wander at the same time. A herd can consist of a few animals or of many thousands. For wolves people say pack, and for fish and birds **flock** or shoal.

In a herd, many animals see and hear at the same time whether an enemy is coming. When one animal notices danger, often the whole group flees together. For a predator it is hard to pick out a single animal from a dense group. In the crowd, each individual animal has a smaller risk of being caught. In winter, some herd animals also warm each other.

In most herds there is a **ranking order**, which decides who eats first or gets the best place. Often there is a **lead animal**, in cattle usually an experienced cow. At the move up to the Alpine pastures in Switzerland, the lead cow often goes in front and wears an especially large bell. Among the Eringer cows in the Valais, cow fights decide which cow is the queen of the herd. Once the ranking order is settled, the animals mostly live together peacefully.

The largest herds are formed by the **wildebeest** in East Africa, which, with zebras and gazelles, wander every year through the Serengeti and the Masai Mara. In doing so, well over a million animals follow the rains and the fresh grass. In North America, enormous herds of bison with millions of animals once lived. Reindeer travel in large herds in the far north. In the Alps, ibex and chamois live in smaller groups.

For thousands of years, humans have kept herds of farm animals. Herdswomen and **herdsmen** accompany the animals to the pasture and watch over them. Herding dogs such as the Border Collie help to keep the herd together. In Switzerland, livestock guardian dogs and fences protect many herds from wolves. In summer, large herds go up to the Alpine pastures, and in autumn they return to the valley, decorated, at the move down from the Alps.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of animals of the same species that lives together.
An experienced animal that the others follow.
The order of who is stronger in a group and is allowed first.
A person who looks after and protects a herd.

gewusst: Cows in a herd often lie down to ruminate almost at the same time.
In wildebeest, the calves can run along with the herd only a few minutes after birth.
The word “herd” is also used for people who simply follow the crowd.

teile.einleitung: The hoof is the hard part at the bottom of the foot of a horse, donkey or zebra. It consists of horn and protects the end of the leg like a firm shoe. Without healthy hooves, a horse cannot walk properly.
wichtigste: The hoof is the hard horn shoe at the bottom of a horse's foot.
It consists of keratin, like our fingernails.
Horses actually walk on the tip of a single toe.
Cows, goats and sheep have two toes, which are called cloven hooves.
The hoof keeps growing, about a centimetre a month.
The frog on the underside cushions the shocks when walking.
A farrier looks after the hooves and shoes them with horseshoes.

abschnitte.text: A **hoof** is a hard shoe of horn that encloses the end of the toe. Horses, donkeys and zebras have only one toe with a hoof on each leg, and they are called **odd-toed ungulates**. Cattle, goats, sheep, deer and pigs have two toes, and they are called even-toed ungulates and their hooves cloven hooves. All animals with hooves together are called ungulates.

From the outside you see the hard **hoof wall**, which in the horse runs obliquely downwards at the front. On the underside lie the sole and the wedge-shaped, softer **frog**. The frog acts like a shock absorber and helps to pump blood up through the leg. Inside sit bones, tendons and well-supplied tissue that nourishes the hoof.

Like a fingernail, the hoof keeps growing, in the horse about a centimetre a month. Wild horses cover long distances on hard ground and in doing so wear down their hooves by themselves. In domestic horses, the hoof therefore has to be trimmed every six to eight weeks. Because there are no nerves in the outer horn, trimming does not hurt.

Many riding and working horses wear **horseshoes**, which protect the hoof from too much wear. They are fixed to the hoof wall with nails by the farrier, without the horse feeling pain. There are also hoof boots to put on or fittings made of plastic. An old horseshoe is regarded by many people as a lucky charm.

Horse keepers pick out the hooves regularly with a **hoof pick**, so that no stones and no dirt get stuck. A wet, dirty stable can cause rot in the frog. A serious illness is laminitis, in which the tissue in the hoof becomes inflamed. That is why people who work with horses say that a horse is only as good as its hooves.

begriffe.erklaerung: The hard horn shoe on the foot of horses and other ungulates.
The soft, wedge-shaped part on the underside of a horse's hoof.
A hoofed animal with an odd number of toes, for example horses.
The two-part hooves of cows, goats and sheep.

gewusst: In essence, a horse walks on the tip of its middle finger, or rather its middle toe.
It takes about a year for a horse's hoof to grow out completely from top to bottom.
The ancestors of horses still had several toes on each foot.

teile.einleitung: Honeybees are insects that live together in large colonies and make honey. A colony consists of a queen, many thousands of workers and, in summer, a few hundred drones. Honeybees are very important for humans, because they pollinate flowers and so provide fruit and vegetables.
wichtigste: In summer a bee colony has up to about 50,000 bees.
The queen lays all the eggs in the colony.
Workers collect food, build honeycombs and look after the queen.
Drones are the male bees.
With the waggle dance, bees show each other where there is food.
Honeybees pollinate many fruit trees and crop plants.
The varroa mite is a great danger for bee colonies.

abschnitte.text: A worker is about 12 to 15 millimetres long, has a hairy body and brown to yellowish stripes. On the hind legs she carries **pollen baskets** in which she collects pollen. With her proboscis she sucks up nectar. At the rear of the abdomen she has a sting with barbs, which stays stuck in the skin of humans, which is why the bee dies after the sting.

At the centre is the **queen**, who in summer can lay up to about 2,000 eggs a day. The workers are also females, but normally do not lay eggs. The **drones** are males whose only task is mating with young queens. In late summer they are driven out of the hive by the workers.

A worker changes her tasks with age. Young bees clean cells, feed the larvae and build new honeycombs with wax from their body. After that they guard the entrance of the hive. Only in the last phase of their life do they fly out as forager bees and fetch nectar, pollen and water, and in summer they live only about five to six weeks.

When a forager bee has found a good source of food, she dances on the comb in the hive. In the **waggle dance**, the direction of the dance shows the direction to the food source, and its duration reveals the distance. This was discovered by the Austrian researcher Karl von Frisch. For it he received the Nobel Prize in 1973.

Honeybees supply honey and wax and pollinate apple, cherry and pear trees as well as many other plants. Without pollination, many fruits would not grow at all or would only grow small. Dangerous for the colonies are the introduced **varroa mite**, diseases, pesticides and a lack of flowers. In Switzerland, the dark bee is the originally native subspecies, which beekeepers today are in part deliberately breeding again.

begriffe.erklaerung: The only female in the colony that lays eggs.
A male honeybee without a sting.
The transfer of pollen so that plants form fruit and seeds.
A tiny parasite that weakens bees and their brood.

gewusst: Bees can see ultraviolet light, which is invisible to humans.
Drones have no sting and therefore cannot sting.
In winter the bees form a dense cluster and keep themselves warm by shivering their muscles.

teile.einleitung: The great crested newt is the largest newt in Switzerland and in central Europe. It gets its name from the tall, jagged crest that the males carry on their backs in spring. It has become rare and is seriously threatened in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The great crested newt is known scientifically as Triturus cristatus.
It grows to about 18 centimetres long.
Like the alpine newt it belongs to the newts, but it grows a much taller crest.
Its belly is yellow to orange with black spots.
It needs ponds with plenty of water plants and without fish.
In Switzerland it is classed as seriously threatened.
In Ticino lives the closely related Italian crested newt.

abschnitte.text: The **great crested newt** is a tailed amphibian with dark brown to black, warty skin that is finely speckled with white. The belly glows yellow to orange and has black spots, whose pattern is different on every animal. Females grow to about 18 centimetres long, males are slightly smaller. In spring the males grow a tall, deeply jagged **crest** on the back, which is interrupted at the base of the tail. On the tail they then carry a silvery-white stripe.

The great crested newt lives in large parts of Europe, from France to Russia. In Switzerland it occurs mainly on the Central Plateau and at low altitudes north of the Alps. It needs sunny, plant-rich **ponds** and pools in which no fish live, because fish eat its larvae. Outside the breeding season it lives on land in damp woods and meadows and hides under wood and stones.

In the water, great crested newts eat insect larvae, small crustaceans, worms, snails and tadpoles. On land they hunt earthworms, woodlice and insects. They hunt mainly at dusk and at night. Their own larvae sometimes even eat the larvae of other newts.

In spring, great crested newts migrate to their **breeding water**. The male performs a courtship dance and wafts scents towards the female with his tail. The female lays each egg singly and carefully wraps it in a leaf of a water plant. The eggs hatch into larvae with feathery **external gills**, which turn into small newts by late summer.

Many ponds and wetlands have been drained or filled in, which is why the great crested newt has become rare. Fish put into ponds and roads where the animals are run over also threaten it. In Switzerland it is listed as seriously threatened on the **Red List**. Nature conservation organisations create new, fish-free ponds in which the newts can breed again.

begriffe.erklaerung: An amphibian with a tail that lives in water and on land.
An animal that lives in water as a larva and later on land as well, for example a frog or a newt.
Feather-like breathing organs that sit on the outside of the head in newt larvae.
A body of water in which amphibians lay their eggs.
A list of threatened animal and plant species.

gewusst: Because the spot pattern on the belly is unique like a fingerprint, researchers can recognise individual great crested newts in photos.
In the wild, great crested newts can live for more than ten years.

teile.einleitung: The Chamois Coloured goat, in German Gämsfarbige Gebirgsziege, is a Swiss goat breed and the most common goat breed in the country. It is brown like a chamois and has a black stripe on its back. As a hardy dairy goat, it is as much at home in the mountains as in the lowlands.
wichtigste: The Chamois Coloured goat is a breed of domestic goat from Switzerland.
It is the most common goat breed in Switzerland.
Its coat is brown with a black stripe on the back.
The belly and legs are also coloured black.
It is kept mainly for its milk.
It is hardy, undemanding and well adapted to life in the mountains.
In North America, a related breed is called the Oberhasli.

abschnitte.text: The Chamois Coloured goat has a short, reddish brown to chestnut coat. A black **dorsal stripe** runs over the back, as in many wild animals. The belly and lower legs are black, so it looks as if it were wearing black boots. It also has black stripes on the face. This colouring is reminiscent of the wild **chamois**, hence the name.

The breed comes from the Swiss Alps, above all from Graubünden and the Bernese Oberland. Today it is bred throughout Switzerland. It is the largest **goat breed** in the country by number. It is also kept in other countries, for example in Germany, Austria and the USA.

The Chamois Coloured goat is above all a **dairy goat**. A good doe gives several hundred litres of milk a year. From goat's milk people make cheese, yoghurt and fresh cheese, for example the popular goat's fresh cheese. In part the meat of the young animals, the kids, is also eaten. Goats also help to keep steep Alpine pastures open, because they eat bushes and shrubs.

The breed is adapted to the rough mountain climate. It climbs surely in steep terrain and manages on sparse food. Goats eat grass, herbs, leaves and twigs. They are curious and intelligent animals that live in a **herd**. Some animals carry horns, others are naturally hornless.

In Switzerland there are several native goat breeds, for example the Saanen goat, the Toggenburg goat and the Valais Blackneck goat. The Chamois Coloured goat is the most common among them. Breeding is supported by the **Swiss Goat Breeders' Association**. Breeders pay attention to health, milk yield and the typical colour. The female is called a doe, the male a buck and the young a kid.

begriffe.erklaerung: A dark stripe that runs down the middle of the back.
A group of domestic animals of one species with shared features.
The Swiss word for a young kid.
A goat that is kept mainly for its milk.

gewusst: Goats were among the first animals that humans turned into domestic animals, about 10,000 years ago.
Goats can pluck individual leaves very skilfully with their lips.
In North America the Chamois Coloured goat is known under the name Oberhasli, after a region in the Bernese Oberland.

teile.einleitung: Keeping a dog means taking a dog in and caring for it. A dog is not a toy but a member of the family that needs time, money and attention for many years. In Switzerland there are clear rules for this to protect animals.
wichtigste: The keeper makes sure that the dog gets enough to eat and drink.
A dog needs enough exercise every day to stay healthy and content.
Dogs need contact with humans or other dogs every day.
In Switzerland, every dog must have a microchip and be registered.
For dogs you generally pay a dog tax.
You have to pick up dog mess on the way and dispose of it.
Over its whole life a dog costs a lot of money for food and vet.

abschnitte.text: Before a dog moves in, the whole family should think carefully. A dog often lives 10 to 15 years and needs time every day. You have to ask yourself who will walk it and who will look after it during the holidays. The **breed** is also important, because a herding dog needs much more occupation than a placid companion dog. Many dogs are also waiting in an **animal shelter** for a new home.

The keeper makes sure that the dog gets suitable food and always fresh water. Depending on the breed, the coat has to be brushed regularly. Claws, ears and teeth are also checked. Once a year you go to the **vet** for vaccinations and a check-up. Against worms, fleas and ticks there are treatments that the vet recommends.

A dog needs several walks in the fresh air every day. In doing so it sniffs, meets other dogs and experiences new things. Brain work is also important, for example search games, **retrieving** or small tricks. A dog that is bored often barks a lot or chews things in the home. Dogs are pack animals and should not be alone all day.

The **Animal Welfare Act** requires that dogs get sufficient outdoor exercise every day and contact with humans. Every dog must be marked with a microchip and registered in the **AMICUS** database. The municipalities charge a dog tax. In many cantons, liability insurance for dogs is compulsory. Some cantons have additional rules, for example for large breeds or breeds classed as dangerous.

abschnitte.titel: Out and about with the dog
abschnitte.text: When out and about, you show consideration for other people and animals. You pick up the **dog mess** with a bag and put it in a rubbish bin. In the woods and on meadows with cows or wild animals, you keep the dog on a lead. Many cantons require dogs to be on a lead in the woods in spring and early summer, because that is when young wild animals are born. On buses and trains a large dog needs its own ticket.

A dog costs money not only when you buy it. Every month there is food, and in addition vet, insurance, dog tax and accessories such as lead and basket. A **dog school** or care during the holidays also cost something. Over a whole dog's life, several thousand francs quickly add up.

begriffe.erklaerung: A person who is responsible for a dog and has it with them.
A tiny chip under the skin with a number through which the owner can be found.
A law that regulates how humans must treat animals well.
Insurance that pays if the dog causes damage to others.

gewusst: Large dogs need a half-price ticket on Swiss trains, and small dogs in a bag travel free.
Many animal shelters in Switzerland place dogs only after a get-to-know-you visit.
A dog that gets enough exercise often sleeps 12 to 14 hours a day.

teile.einleitung: The Canada goose is a large goose with a black neck and a white patch on the chin and cheeks. It originally comes from North America, but was brought to Europe by people. Today you can also see it here at lakes, in parks and on meadows.
wichtigste: The Canada goose is known scientifically as Branta canadensis.
It originally comes from North America.
In Europe it was introduced by people, first in England.
It is the largest goose living wild in Europe.
Typical is the white chinstrap on the black head.
Canada geese eat mainly grass, herbs and water plants.
In Switzerland it is a non-native breeding bird.

abschnitte.text: The **Canada goose** has a brownish-grey body, a long black neck and a black head. Striking is the broad white **chinstrap** that runs from the throat to the cheeks. It grows to about 90 to 110 centimetres long and can weigh over 5 kilograms. Its wingspan is up to about 1.8 metres. Males and females look the same.

The Canada goose originally lives in **North America**, from Alaska and Canada to the USA. As early as the 17th century, Canada geese were kept in parks in England, and from there they spread. Today large populations live in Great Britain, Scandinavia, the Netherlands and Germany. In Switzerland only a small number breed, but you can see them at large lakes and rivers. Because it was introduced by people, it is a **neozoon** here.

Canada geese are **herbivores**. They graze on meadows, lawns and fields and also eat water plants, seeds and grain. With their beaks they can crop grass close to the ground. In parks they sometimes let themselves be fed, which is harmful to the birds and to the water.

Canada geese often live with the same partner all their lives. The female usually lays five to six eggs in a nest of plants and down close to the water. Both parents defend their young bravely, hissing loudly and even attacking people who come too close. In North America many Canada geese fly south in autumn in large **V-formations**, whereas most European birds stay in their area all year round.

Where very many Canada geese live, their droppings foul sunbathing lawns, bathing beaches and waters. They can also drive out native waterbirds and cause damage in fields. That is why experts watch their spread closely, and in some countries their numbers are controlled. In Switzerland it counts as a **non-native species**, whose numbers are monitored and, if necessary, controlled.

begriffe.erklaerung: An animal that has reached a new area through human action.
The white patch on the throat and cheeks of the Canada goose.
A flying pattern in the shape of a V that saves migrating birds energy.
An animal that feeds only or almost only on plants.

gewusst: When flying in V-formation, the geese take turns at the front, because the leading bird needs the most strength.
Young Canada geese can swim and find food themselves just one day after hatching.

teile.einleitung: Armadillos are mammals from the Americas that wear a hard armour of bony plates. They have their name from the movable cross bands in the middle of the armour, which look like belts. Their ancestors, the glyptodonts, were as big as a small car.
wichtigste: Armadillos belong to the superorder of the xenarthrans, together with sloths and anteaters.
Within this group they form the order Cingulata.
Today about 20 living species of armadillo are distinguished.
Their armour consists of bony plates covered with horny scales.
Since genetic studies around 2016, they have been divided into the families Dasypodidae and Chlamyphoridae.
Armadillos live in South and Central America and in the south of North America.
They eat mainly insects such as ants, termites and larvae.

abschnitte.text: The armour of an armadillo consists of **bony plates** over which lie horny scales. At the front over the shoulders and at the back over the pelvis sits a rigid shield. Between them lie movable **cross bands** joined by soft skin, which is why the German name is Gürteltier, “belt animal”. The Spanish word “armadillo” means “little armoured one”.

There are about 20 species of armadillo living today. The largest is the **giant armadillo**, which can grow to about 1.5 metres long with its tail. The smallest is the **pink fairy armadillo** from Argentina, which measures only about 10 to 12 centimetres and is coloured pink. The most widespread is the nine-banded armadillo.

Armadillos live from the south of the USA to Argentina, in forests, savannahs, grassland and semi-deserts. With their strong **digging claws** they dig burrows and look for food in the ground. They eat mainly ants, termites, beetles and larvae, and some also eat fruit, small animals or carrion. They see badly, but smell very well.

Armadillos belong to the **xenarthrans** (Xenarthra), a very old group of mammals from South America. The name refers to extra joints on the lumbar vertebrae, which make the spine more stable. Their closest relatives are the sloths and the anteaters. Since 2016 the armadillos have been divided into two families: Dasypodidae and Chlamyphoridae.

About 10,000 years ago, the **glyptodonts**, huge armoured animals, still lived in the Americas. Some reached about the size of a small car. Studies of ancient DNA showed that they belong to today's armadillo family Chlamyphoridae. The glyptodont **Doedicurus** even had a tail club with a bony armour, which it probably used as a weapon.

begriffe.erklaerung: The scientific name of the xenarthrans, to which armadillos, sloths and anteaters belong.
Extinct, giant relatives of the armadillos with an armour like a tortoise shell.
Long, strong claws with which animals dig in the ground.
A group of closely related animal species.

gewusst: The nine-banded armadillo almost always gives birth to identical quadruplets.
Only the three-banded armadillos can roll up completely into a firm ball.
The mascot of the 2014 football World Cup in Brazil was a three-banded armadillo.

teile.einleitung: Hay is dried grass with herbs and flowers from the meadow. In winter it is the most important feed for cows, sheep, goats and horses, when hardly any fresh green grows outside. Without hay, many farm animals could not get through the winter well in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Hay is grass that has been dried in the sun after mowing.
In winter, sheep, cows, goats and horses eat mainly hay.
Dry hay does not go mouldy and can be stored for months.
The second cut of a meadow is called “Emd” in Switzerland.
Rabbits and guinea pigs need hay for their digestion and their teeth.
Damp hay can heat up so strongly that it starts to burn.
In steep mountain areas, wild hay is still mown by hand in some places today.

abschnitte.text: Hay consists of grasses, herbs and flowers from a meadow that have been mown and dried. In drying, the grass loses most of its water. Good hay is greenish, smells pleasantly spicy and is not dusty. The scent of fresh hay in particular reminds many people of summer in the countryside.

In early summer the farmer mows the meadow with the **mower** on the tractor. Then the grass is turned several times so that it dries well on all sides. After two to three sunny days it is raked together into long rows, the **swaths**. Finally the hay is brought in loose or pressed into large bales.

Ruminants such as cows, sheep and goats need a lot of fibre so that their stomach works properly. Hay supplies exactly this **crude fibre**. In winter, when the pastures are under snow, hay is therefore their main feed. Horses, donkeys, rabbits and guinea pigs also eat a lot of hay, because chewing wears down their constantly growing teeth.

Hay is stored dry in the **hayloft** or in a barn. If it is still too damp when stored, it starts to go mouldy or ferment. It can then get so hot that it ignites by itself. Such hay fires have already destroyed whole farms, so farmers often measure the temperature in the haystack.

Many Swiss meadows are mown several times a year. The first cut gives the hay, the second the **Emd**, which is finer and richer in nutrients. In the mountains there are wild hay farmers who still mow steep slopes with a scythe where no machine can reach. Milk from cows that eat only grass and hay is sold as hay milk.

begriffe.erklaerung: The Swiss word for the hay from the second cut of a meadow.
A long row of mown grass that is raked together in the field.
Hard plant fibres that ruminants need for digestion.
Grass that is not dried but packed airtight and fermented.

gewusst: Hay fever has nothing to do with hay, but is triggered by flower pollen.
The saying “looking for a needle in a haystack” means that something is almost impossible to find.
Fresh grass consists for the most part of water, so much less weight is left after drying.

teile.einleitung: Honey is a sweet, viscous food that honeybees make from the nectar of flowers or from honeydew. The bees store it in their honeycombs as a supply for the winter. Humans have eaten honey since the Stone Age and value it as a natural sweetener.
wichtigste: Bees make honey from flower nectar or honeydew.
Honey is mostly golden yellow to brown.
For some honey, bees have to visit very many flowers, often thousands.
In winter, the bees live on the stored honey.
Honey consists for the most part of sugar and contains little water.
Almost every honey becomes solid over time, it crystallises.
Babies under one year should not eat honey.

abschnitte.text: Honey is a store that honeybees lay in for times when nothing is in flower. It consists of about four fifths of various sugars, above all **fructose** and glucose. In addition there are water and small amounts of minerals, proteins and aromatic substances. Depending on the plant, honey is pale yellow, golden yellow, brown or almost black.

Forager bees suck **nectar** out of flowers with their proboscis and carry it to the hive in their honey stomach. As they do so, they add substances from their body that change the sugar. In the hive they pass the nectar on to other bees, which fill it into the honeycomb cells. By fanning with their wings, water evaporates until the honey is thick, and then they seal the cells with a wax cap.

**Blossom honey** comes from the nectar of flowers, fruit trees, oilseed rape or lime trees. Forest honey comes from honeydew that aphids excrete on trees, and is mostly dark and strong. Some kinds become solid quickly, such as rape honey, while others, such as acacia honey, stay liquid for a long time. Becoming solid is called **crystallising** and is not a sign of poor quality.

Even in the Stone Age, people took honey from wild bees' nests, as an old rock painting in Spain shows. The ancient Egyptians already kept bees and placed honey in tombs as a grave offering. Until sugar from sugar cane and sugar beet became cheap, honey was the most important sweetener in Europe. That is why it was long something valuable.

Honey hardly spoils, because it contains very little water and a lot of sugar, so bacteria grow poorly in it. You eat it on bread, in tea or use it for baking, for example for gingerbread and Biberli, a Swiss spiced pastry. Babies under one year should not eat honey, because it can contain rare bacteria that are dangerous for them. In Switzerland, many **beekeepers** produce their own honey, but a large part of the honey is imported.

begriffe.erklaerung: Sweet juice in flowers that attracts insects.
A wall of many hexagonal wax cells in the beehive.
When liquid honey becomes solid and grainy.
A person who keeps and looks after bees.

gewusst: Properly stored honey stays edible for years.
For a single jar of honey, bees have to fly out many thousands of times.
The colour and taste of honey reveal which plants it comes from.

teile.einleitung: The great green bush cricket is one of the largest grasshoppers in Switzerland. It is grass green, has long antennae and sings loudly from bushes and trees on warm summer evenings. Unlike what you might think, it eats mainly other insects.
wichtigste: The great green bush cricket is a large bush cricket that occurs in Switzerland.
It is green and grows to about 3 to 4 centimetres long.
Its antennae are longer than its whole body.
It eats mainly insects such as aphids, flies and caterpillars.
The males sing from July into autumn, often into the night.
Its ears sit on the front legs.
The females have a long ovipositor on the abdomen.

abschnitte.text: The great green bush cricket is called **Tettigonia viridissima** in science, which means roughly “the greenest”. It grows to about 3 to 4 centimetres long and is bright grass green, sometimes with a brownish stripe on its back. Its wings are longer than the abdomen, and the thin **antennae** even extend beyond the whole body. The females carry a long, sabre-shaped **ovipositor** on the abdomen. With its strong hind legs it can jump far and also fly well.

The great green bush cricket lives in large parts of Europe, in North Africa and in parts of Asia. It likes hedges, woodland edges, bushes, orchards, grain fields and also gardens in towns. In Switzerland it is common mainly at lower altitudes. Because it is so well camouflaged in green, you usually hear it rather than see it. It often sits high up in trees and shrubs.

The great green bush cricket is above all a **predator**. It eats flies, caterpillars, aphids, beetle larvae and other small insects. Plant parts such as leaves or flowers are sometimes added. Because it eats many pests, it is a useful helper in the garden. If you handle it carelessly, it can also pinch with its strong mouthparts.

The males sing from about July to October, especially in the afternoon and until late at night. To do so they rub their front wings against each other: a toothed **file** on one wing strokes over an edge on the other. This produces a loud, whirring chirp that can be heard from far away. The song is heard with ears on the front legs, the **tympanal organs**. This is how the females find the singing male.

In late summer the female lays her eggs one by one into the soil with her ovipositor. The eggs overwinter, and some even need several years before the larvae hatch. The young bush crickets look like small adults without wings. They moult several times and grow as they do, until they are adult in high summer. This development without a pupa is called **incomplete metamorphosis**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A jumping insect with strong hind legs that often chirps.
Grasshoppers with very long antennae, to which the great green bush cricket belongs.
A long extension on the abdomen with which the female lays eggs into the soil.
The hearing organ of the grasshopper, on the front legs in the bush cricket.

gewusst: The long antennae of the bush cricket are longer than its whole body and serve for touching and smelling.
Despite its German name Heupferd, “hay horse”, it hardly eats any hay, but mainly other insects.
In German it is also called the Grünes Heupferd, “green hay horse”, and its ovipositor is not dangerous, because it cannot sting with it.

teile.einleitung: Kanzi was a bonobo who became world-famous because he could communicate with people using symbols. He lived in the USA in a research centre and showed how much great apes can learn about language. His story has strongly influenced research into animal intelligence.
wichtigste: Kanzi was a male bonobo, a species of great ape.
He was born in the USA in 1980.
He learned to communicate using picture symbols on a keyboard.
He also understood many spoken English words and sentences.
The scientist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh did most of the research with him.
Kanzi even made simple stone tools.
He died in March 2025 at the age of 44.

abschnitte.text: Kanzi was a **bonobo**, a great ape that is closely related to the chimpanzee. He was born in 1980 in a research centre in the US state of Georgia. He grew up with his adoptive mother Matata. Later he lived in a sanctuary for great apes in Des Moines in the state of Iowa.

Bonobos cannot pronounce words, because their larynx is built differently. So the researchers used a board with **lexigrams**, which are picture symbols that stand for words. By pressing a symbol, Kanzi could say what he wanted, for example banana or go outside. In the end he knew several hundred such symbols.

Actually Kanzi’s mother Matata was supposed to learn the symbols, but she found it hard. Little Kanzi was only present at the lessons and watched. One day it turned out that he had learned the symbols entirely by himself, in the same way that children learn their **mother tongue**. That was an important discovery for research.

Kanzi also understood spoken English astonishingly well. In tests he carried out new requests that he had never heard before, for example to put an object in a particular place. The researcher **Sue Savage-Rumbaugh** compared his understanding of language with that of a child of about two. Other experts were more cautious about such comparisons.

Kanzi also learned to strike stones against one another to make sharp **flakes**. With these he cut through strings to get at food in a box. Researchers wanted to find out in this way how the first stone tools of early humans might have come about. Kanzi also found his own ways, for example by throwing stones onto the ground.

In the wild, bonobos live only in the rainforests of the **Democratic Republic of the Congo** in Africa, south of the Congo River. They are classed as endangered, because their forest is being cut down and they are hunted. Together with chimpanzees, they are the closest living relatives of humans. Kanzi’s life has shown many people how clever and special these animals are.

begriffe.erklaerung: A great ape from Africa, closely related to the chimpanzee.
A picture symbol that stands for a particular word.
The science that studies monkeys and apes.
A sharp piece of stone that is struck off a larger stone.

gewusst: Kanzi liked to play Pac-Man and other simple video games.
Kanzi did not learn the symbols in lessons, but just by watching.

teile.einleitung: Sharks are predatory fish that have lived in the seas for over 400 million years, long before the dinosaurs. There are over 500 species, from the tiny lantern shark to the giant whale shark. Most sharks are harmless to humans, but many species are themselves severely threatened.
wichtigste: Sharks have existed for over 400 million years.
Their skeleton consists not of bone but of cartilage.
There are over 500 species of shark, and most are harmless to humans.
If a shark loses a tooth, a new one grows in.
Sharks have very fine senses and can even sense the electrical signals of their prey.
Many species are threatened by overfishing.
In Switzerland there are no wild sharks, and you see them only in zoos and aquariums.

abschnitte.text: Sharks belong to the **cartilaginous fish**, so their skeleton is flexible and light. Their skin is covered with tiny skin teeth and feels like sandpaper. Many sharks are dark on top and pale underneath, and this camouflage is called **countershading**. From above you can hardly see them against the dark water, and from below you cannot see them against the bright sky either.

The largest shark and at the same time the largest fish is the **whale shark**, which can grow to over 12 metres long. Despite its size it eats only plankton and small fish. The great white shark reaches about 6 metres in length. The smallest sharks, such as the dwarf lantern shark, are by contrast only about 20 centimetres long.

Sharks smell very well and sense movements in the water with the **lateral line organ**. With the **ampullae of Lorenzini** on the snout they perceive the weak electric fields that every living thing produces. They breathe through gills, which they have at the sides of the head. Some species have to keep swimming constantly so that enough water flows over the gills, otherwise they get too little oxygen.

Sharks have several rows of teeth one behind the other, like a **revolving set of teeth**. When a tooth falls out, a new one moves up, so a shark uses up thousands of teeth in its life. Depending on the species, the young are born alive or hatch from eggs. Many species have only a few young, often fewer than ten, and the mother mostly does not look after them, as the young are independent at once.

Attacks by sharks on humans are **very rare**, almost negligible compared with other dangers such as road accidents. Conversely, humans kill many millions of sharks every year, often only for their fins for shark fin soup. Because sharks grow slowly and have few young, their populations recover only with difficulty. Many species are therefore threatened today and are protected by conservation agreements.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fish with a skeleton of cartilage instead of bone, for example sharks and rays.
Camouflage through a dark upper side and a pale underside.
Sense organs on the head of sharks with which they sense electric fields.
When more fish are caught than can grow back.

gewusst: The Greenland shark can probably live to be several hundred years old and is thus one of the longest-lived vertebrates.
Sharks have no swim bladder, and their large, oil-rich liver helps them to float in the water.
The extinct megalodon was a giant shark that probably grew to well over 10 metres long.

teile.einleitung: A stallion is an adult male horse that has not been castrated. Stallions are often powerful, spirited and important for breeding. In a wild herd of horses, the stallion protects his group.
wichtigste: A stallion is an adult male horse that has not been castrated.
A castrated male horse is called a gelding.
The female horse is called a mare, the young horse a foal.
In wild herds, a stallion often lives together with several mares.
Young stallions join together in bachelor groups.
Stallions chosen for breeding are called breeding stallions.
In donkeys and zebras too, the male is called a stallion.

abschnitte.text: A **stallion** is a male horse that is sexually mature and not castrated. A young male horse is called a colt. If a stallion is castrated, he is called a **gelding**. Geldings are usually calmer and are therefore often used as riding horses. Male donkeys and zebras are also called stallions.

Stallions often have a stronger neck and a more muscular body than mares. Usually only male horses have clearly visible **tushes**, small pointed teeth behind the incisors. Stallions are often spirited and want to show their strength. To pick up smells better, they curl back the upper lip, which is called the **flehmen response**. Between rivals there are threatening displays, rearing and sometimes fights.

In wild horses, a stallion often lives together with several mares and their foals. He protects the group and rounds it up in danger. Leading the way to water or to pasture is often done by an experienced mare. Young stallions leave the family and live in **bachelor groups**. Only when they are strong enough do they found a family of their own.

For breeding, especially healthy and well-built stallions are chosen, which is called **licensing**. These breeding stallions pass on their qualities to many foals. In Switzerland, the **national stud farm** in Avenches looks after the breeding of Freiberger stallions. Also famous are the white Lipizzaner stallions of the Spanish Riding School in Vienna. If you cross a male donkey with a mare, a mule is the result.

Stallions need experienced keepers, because they are strong and sometimes difficult. They are often kept apart from mares so that there are no unplanned foals. Even so, like all horses they need contact with others of their kind and plenty of exercise. In Switzerland, animal welfare law requires that horses do not live completely alone. Many stallions are ridden successfully in sport, for example in show jumping and dressage.

begriffe.erklaerung: A castrated male horse.
An adult female horse.
The test of whether a stallion is suitable for breeding.
Curling back the upper lip to check smells better.

gewusst: A single breeding stallion can become the father of hundreds of foals in the course of his life.
Lipizzaners are born dark and only turn white over the years.
A mule has a donkey father and a horse mother, while a hinny has a horse father and a donkey mother.

teile.einleitung: Domestic cattle are large hoofed animals that humans have kept for about 10,000 years. They provide milk, meat and leather, and in the past they were also used as draught animals. Domestic cattle include cows, bulls, oxen and calves.
wichtigste: Domestic cattle descend from the wild aurochs.
The cow gives us milk, which we drink or make into cheese.
A male bovine is called a bull, a castrated one an ox and the young a calf.
Cattle are ruminants with a stomach in four parts.
There are about a billion domestic cattle worldwide.
On Swiss farms, cattle are the most important farm animals.
Cattle like to live in herds with a fixed ranking order.

abschnitte.text: The wild ancestor of domestic cattle is the **aurochs**, a mighty wild bovine with large horns. About 10,000 years ago, people in the Middle East began to tame and breed aurochs. A little later the **zebu** with its typical hump arose in India. The last wild aurochs died in 1627 in a forest in Poland. In its descendants, the domestic cattle, it lives on to this day, however.

Adult domestic cattle weigh, depending on the breed, between about 400 kilograms and over a tonne. The male animal is called a **bull**, the castrated male an ox. The female animal is called a cow after her first calf, before that a heifer. Cattle are **even-toed ungulates**, because they walk on two toes per leg. Many breeds carry horns, which grow throughout life.

Most important today is **milk**, from which butter, cream, yoghurt and cheese are made. Cattle also provide meat, for example beef and veal. From their hide comes **leather** for shoes and bags. In the past, oxen pulled ploughs and carts, and in some countries they still do so today. The manure of cattle serves as a valuable fertiliser for the fields.

Cattle eat grass, hay, silage and other plants. They are **ruminants** and have a stomach with four parts: rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum. In the rumen, tiny living things help to break down the tough grass. In the process the gas **methane** is produced, which the cattle belch out and which contributes to global warming. That is why researchers are looking for feed that produces less methane.

About 1.5 million cattle live in Switzerland (as of around 2023). Well-known breeds are the **Brown Swiss**, the Simmental Fleckvieh, the Holstein cow and the Eringer cow from the Valais. Many cattle spend the summer on Alpine pastures, where flavourful Alpine cheese is made. Switzerland has strict animal welfare rules, for example for outdoor access and space in the shed. Cow's milk is the basis for world-famous cheeses such as Emmental.

begriffe.erklaerung: An extinct wild bovine from which all domestic cattle descend.
A hoofed animal that walks on two toes per leg, like cattle, sheep, goats and pigs.
A castrated male bovine that was often used as a draught animal in the past.
A gas that is produced during digestion in the stomach of cattle and warms the climate.

gewusst: Cattle have a pattern of lines on the nose that is as unique as a human fingerprint.
In India, cows are regarded as sacred in Hinduism and may roam freely along many streets.
Cattle can see colours, but red only poorly, so a bull reacts more to the movement of the cloth than to its colour.

teile.einleitung: Livestock guardian dogs are large, powerful dogs that live day and night with a herd and protect it from predators. In Switzerland they guard above all sheep and goats on the Alpine pastures from wolves. They are not herding dogs but real guards.
wichtigste: Livestock guardian dogs are dogs that protect farm animals from wolves.
In Switzerland, farmers often protect their sheep with specially trained livestock guardian dogs.
Livestock guardian dogs grow up with the herd from a young age.
They drive wolves away by barking and threatening.
Herding dogs drive a herd, while livestock guardian dogs guard it.
Together with fences, they help to reduce conflicts between wolves and Alpine farming.
Llamas, alpacas or donkeys are also sometimes used to protect herds.

abschnitte.text: **Livestock guardian dogs** are large breeds of dog that guard a herd permanently. They live together with the sheep or goats and regard them as their family. Adult dogs often weigh 40 to 60 kilograms and have a dense, mostly pale coat. In Switzerland, mainly the breeds **Maremmano-Abruzzese** from Italy and Pyrenean Mountain Dog (Montagne des Pyrénées) from France are used. Such dogs have protected herds in southern Europe and Asia for many centuries.

The wolf was long extinct in Switzerland and returned in 1995 from Italy. Since 2012, wolves have also formed **packs** here again, the first on the Calanda in Graubünden. Wolves sometimes kill unprotected sheep and goats. That is why experts promote the use of livestock guardian dogs and **fences** to reduce conflicts between wolves and Alpine farming. The Confederation supports farmers who protect their herds.

Livestock guardian dogs stay with the herd day and night, even in rain and snow. When a wolf, a fox or a strange dog approaches, they bark loudly and place themselves between the herd and the intruder. Usually that is enough for the wolf to move on. The dogs often work in groups of two or more animals. It is important that the puppies grow up with the farm animals early on, so that they develop a close **bond** with the herd.

Livestock guardian dogs also defend their herd against people who come too close. That is why signs on hiking trails point out such dogs. It is best to stay calm, go around the herd at a distance and get off your bike. You should not stroke the dogs, feed them or threaten them with sticks. You put your own dogs on a **lead**, so that there is no quarrel.

Not only dogs can protect a herd. **Llamas**, alpacas and donkeys are also sometimes used for sheep or hens, because they chase away foxes or dogs. In addition, electric fences and night pens protect the animals. Some herds are looked after by herdswomen and herdsmen who are with them all the time. Often a combination of several measures works best.

begriffe.erklaerung: All the measures that protect farm animals from predators.
A dog that drives and holds a herd together, for example the Border Collie.
A family group of wolves.
Keeping animals on mountain pastures in summer.

gewusst: Livestock guardian dogs mostly work independently and do not wait for commands from humans.
A good livestock guardian dog spends almost its whole life outdoors with the animals.
Abroad, people even use ostriches or cattle to warn herds of smaller predators.

teile.einleitung: The Gobi is a huge desert in Central Asia, in Mongolia and the north of China. It is a cold desert with icy winters and hot summers. Rare animals such as the wild camel live here, and famous dinosaur fossils were found in its ground.
wichtigste: The Gobi lies in Mongolia and the north of China.
It is one of the largest deserts in the world and over a million square kilometres in size.
The Gobi is a cold desert with very large differences in temperature.
It consists mostly of stony and gravel desert, and only a small part of sand dunes.
The rare wild camel lives in the Gobi.
The Gobi bear and the reintroduced Przewalski's horse also live there.
The Gobi is famous for dinosaur fossils and fossilised dinosaur eggs.

abschnitte.text: The **Gobi** stretches across the south of Mongolia and Inner Mongolia in the north of China. At over a million square kilometres, it is more than twenty times as big as Switzerland. It lies on a high plateau, mostly about 900 to 1,500 metres above sea level. In the south and west it is bounded by high mountains. These mountains hold back the rain, which is why it is so dry in the Gobi.

The Gobi is a **cold desert**. In winter temperatures drop to below minus 30 degrees, and in summer it can be over 40 degrees hot. The temperature also varies greatly between day and night. Most of it consists not of sand but of stones, gravel and rock, and this is called **stony desert**. But there are also large sand dunes, the singing dunes of Khongoryn Els.

In the Gobi lives the **wild camel**, a Bactrian camel with two humps, which is among the rarest mammals in the world. It can drink salty water, which other camels cannot tolerate. Also very rare is the **Gobi bear**, of which only a few dozen animals are left. Przewalski's horse, a true wild horse, had died out in the wild and was reintroduced to Mongolia from the 1990s. Also living there are goitered gazelles, wild asses, jerboas and, at the edge of the mountains, snow leopards.

The Gobi is one of the most important sites for **dinosaurs** in the world. In the 1920s an American expedition led by Roy Chapman Andrews found fossilised dinosaur eggs here. Famous are the red rocks of Bayanzag, the Flaming Cliffs. There fossils of Protoceratops, Oviraptor and Velociraptor were discovered. Once a Velociraptor and a Protoceratops were even found fossilised locked together in combat.

In the Gobi live mainly **nomads**, who roam with their herds. They keep goats, sheep, camels and horses and live in round felt tents, the yurts. From the wool of the goats the fine cashmere is obtained. In the past, trade routes of the Silk Road ran along the edge of the Gobi. Today, mineral resources such as copper and coal are also mined in the Gobi, which can change nature.

begriffe.erklaerung: A desert with very cold winters, little rain and barren soil.
A desert whose ground consists mainly of stones and gravel.
People who move with their animals from pasture to pasture.
The round felt tent of the Mongolian nomads.
A fossilised remnant of a living thing from prehistoric times.

gewusst: In the Gobi it sometimes snows and freezes in winter, yet it is a true desert because there is so little precipitation.
The wild camel can drink salt water that would be poisonous to most other mammals.
The first scientifically recognised dinosaur eggs were found in the Gobi in the 1920s.

teile.einleitung: Armoured catfish, in German Harnischwelse, are fish from South and Central America that wear an armour of bony plates. With their sucker mouths they hold on to stones and rasp off algae. Many species live in the Amazon, and some are popular aquarium fish with us.
wichtigste: Armoured catfish belong to the catfishes.
They are the catfish family with the most species, with over 900 known species.
They live in rivers and streams of South and Central America, many in the Amazon.
Their body is covered with bony plates like a suit of armour.
With their sucker mouths they hold on even in strong currents.
Many species eat algae, which they rasp off stones and wood.
Well-known aquarium fish are the bristlenose catfish and many so-called L catfish.

abschnitte.text: Instead of scales, armoured catfish have hard **bony plates** that protect their body like a knight's armour. Their belly is flat so that they can lie well on the bottom. The mouth lies on the underside and is shaped into a **sucker mouth**. Depending on the species, they grow from a few centimetres to about one metre long.

Armoured catfish live in fresh waters from Costa Rica and Panama to Argentina. There are particularly many species in the **Amazon basin** and in the Orinoco. Some live in fast-flowing streams with stones, others in slow rivers with dead wood. In some countries such as the USA and in Asia, released armoured catfish have become a pest.

Many armoured catfish are **algae-eaters**: with the small teeth in their sucker mouths they rasp the growth off stones and roots. Others eat small animals, plant remains or mud. Some species of the genus **Panaque** even rasp off wood and take in the fine wood shavings. In the aquarium, some species help to remove algae from glass and stones.

Armoured catfish are often **nocturnal** and hide by day in caves or under roots. In many species the female lays the eggs in a cave. The **male** then guards the clutch, fans fresh water over it and later protects the young fish. Some species can also swallow air when there is a lack of oxygen and take in oxygen through the stomach.

Armoured catfish are very popular with aquarium keepers all over the world. A common aquarium fish is the **bristlenose catfish**, whose males carry small growths on the snout. Many species that did not yet have a scientific name have been given an **L number** since 1988, for example L46 for the zebra pleco. Some species grow very large and therefore need a correspondingly large tank.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mouth with which the fish can hold on like a suction cup.
A large order of fish that mostly have barbels on the mouth.
A number with which aquarium keepers designate armoured catfish without a scientific name.
An animal that is on the move mainly at night.

gewusst: The zebra pleco from Brazil is striped black and white like a zebra.
Some armoured catfish can even climb waterfalls with their sucker mouths.
New species of armoured catfish are still being discovered every year.

teile.einleitung: In a dog school, dogs and their humans learn to get along well together. There they practise commands such as sit and down, but also how to behave properly in everyday life. In fact it is not only the dog that learns, but above all its human too.
wichtigste: In a dog school, dogs train together with their keepers.
When you teach a dog, for example, to sit or lie down, it is called dog training.
People who train dogs for a living are called dog trainers.
Even puppies can learn in special puppy classes.
Dogs learn best with praise and reward.
Besides training there are also sports classes such as agility.
In Switzerland, some cantons require a course for certain dogs.

abschnitte.text: A dog school is a place where **dog trainers** offer courses for dogs and their keepers. Mostly the training takes place outdoors on a fenced area, sometimes also in town or in the woods. Often several dogs train in a group, but there are also one-to-one lessons. The trainer shows the human how to teach something to the dog. After that, practice is done mainly at home in everyday life.

Very young dogs go to a **puppy class**. There they play with other puppies and get to know new sounds, people and places. This early getting used to things is called **socialisation**. After that come young dog classes and training classes for adult dogs. Older dogs, too, can still learn a lot of new things.

Among the most important exercises are **commands** such as sit, down, stay and come. A dog should come back reliably when you call it and walk loosely on the lead. It also learns to stay calm when other dogs, bicycles or children go past. Such rules make living together safer and more relaxed for everyone.

Modern dog trainers rely on **positive reinforcement**. When the dog does something right, it gets a treat, a game or praise straight away. In this way it remembers that this behaviour is worthwhile. Some trainers work with a **clicker**, a small device whose click shows the dog exactly what was right. Punishment and shouting, by contrast, make dogs fearful and confused.

Many dog schools also offer sports. In **agility**, the dog runs through a course with hurdles, tunnels and slalom poles. In mantrailing, it searches with its nose for a hidden person. Further examples are obedience, a kind of obedience gymnastics, and dog dancing with music. Such tasks keep the dog's body and mind fit.

In the past, all new dog keepers in Switzerland had to attend a course. This federal requirement was abolished in 2017. Some cantons, however, still require courses, for example for large or powerful dogs. Experts recommend everyone, especially with a first dog, to attend a good **dog school**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A person who trains dogs and their keepers for a living.
A short word or sign to which the dog is meant to do something particular.
When a young dog learns to deal with humans, animals and new things.
A dog sport in which the dog quickly runs through an obstacle course.

gewusst: The most important learning time of a dog lies in its first months of life.
Dogs often learn commands faster through hand signals than through words.
In agility, faults and time count, and the human runs along and shows the way.

teile.einleitung: Hares are fast mammals with long ears and strong hind legs. In Switzerland live the brown hare and, in the mountains, the mountain hare. Although they look similar, hares and rabbits are different species.
wichtigste: Hares belong to the order of the lagomorphs, not to the rodents.
Hare and rabbit are different species.
Hares have longer ears and longer hind legs than rabbits.
Young hares are born with fur and open eyes.
The brown hare can run at up to about 70 km/h.
Hares do not dig burrows, but rest in a shallow hollow, the form.
In Switzerland the brown hare is considered threatened.

abschnitte.text: The **brown hare** is about 50 to 70 centimetres long and usually weighs 3 to 5 kilograms. Its fur is earth brown, and the long ears have black tips. The strong **hind legs** are much longer than the front legs and make it an excellent runner. Its eyes sit at the sides of the head, so it sees almost all around.

Hares and rabbits are related, but different species that do not mate with each other. Rabbits are smaller, have shorter ears and live in groups in burrows that they dig themselves. Hares mostly live alone in open fields and rest in a shallow hollow, the **form**. Young hares are **precocial** with fur and open eyes, while young rabbits are born naked and blind.

The brown hare lives in open landscapes with meadows, fields, hedges and woodland edges. It eats grasses, herbs, clover, buds and in winter also bark. To get all the nutrients, it eats part of its soft droppings again. Like all **lagomorphs**, it has gnawing teeth that keep growing throughout life.

In danger, the hare presses itself flat into its form and flees only at the last moment. When fleeing, it makes **zigzags**, that is, sudden changes of direction, that shake off foxes and dogs. In spring you can watch hares boxing each other on their hind legs, and often a female is fending off a male. A female has two to four young, usually several times a year.

In Switzerland the brown hare lives mainly on the Central Plateau and in the Jura, and the **mountain hare** in the Alps. The mountain hare has shorter ears and changes its coat in winter from brown to white. The brown hare has become rare in Switzerland and is on the **Red List** as threatened. The reasons are intensive agriculture, missing hedges and fallow land, and road traffic.

begriffe.erklaerung: A shallow hollow in the ground in which the hare rests.
A young animal that can already see and move at birth.
An order of mammals that includes hares, rabbits and pikas.
A list of the animal and plant species that are threatened.

gewusst: A brown hare can jump several metres from a standing start.
The mountain hare is a relic of the Ice Age and lives in Switzerland above the tree line.
The Easter bunny is a hare and not a rabbit, even if it is often drawn that way.

teile.einleitung: The Guinea baboon is the smallest of all baboons and lives in West Africa. It has reddish brown fur and a dark muzzle, and the males carry a mane. Researchers are especially interested in it, because the males behave unusually peacefully towards each other.
wichtigste: The Guinea baboon is the smallest species of baboon.
It lives in West Africa, for example in Senegal, Gambia, Guinea and Guinea-Bissau.
Baboons belong to the Old World monkeys.
Its fur is reddish brown, and the face is bare and dark.
It eats fruit, seeds, grasses, roots and small animals.
Guinea baboons live in large groups with several levels.
The species is considered near threatened.

abschnitte.text: The Guinea baboon has **reddish brown fur** and a long, dog-like muzzle. The face is hairless and dark in colour. The males are clearly larger than the females and carry a mane on the shoulders and neck. Like all **baboons**, they mostly walk on four legs on the ground.

This species of baboon lives in the far west of Africa, in countries such as **Senegal**, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mali and Sierra Leone. There it inhabits **savannahs**, dry forests and gallery forests along rivers. No other baboon lives so far to the west. A well-known research area is Niokolo-Koba National Park in Senegal.

Guinea baboons are **omnivores**. They eat fruit, seeds, leaves, grasses, roots and tubers. Insects and sometimes small vertebrates are added. Because they eat so many things, they cope well with changing seasons and dry seasons.

Guinea baboons live in a **multilevel society**: small family units join together into larger groups. The males are astonishingly tolerant of each other and quarrel much less than in other species of baboon. They greet each other with gestures and communicate with many different sounds. At night the animals sleep in tall trees for protection from enemies.

The Guinea baboon is classed as near threatened by the world conservation union, the **IUCN**. Its habitat is getting smaller because forests are being cleared for fields and settlements. Sometimes the animals are also hunted or persecuted as crop pests. Protected areas such as Niokolo-Koba are therefore important for its survival.

begriffe.erklaerung: Monkeys from Africa and Asia, to which baboons also belong.
An animal that eats both plants and animals.
A warm grassland with scattered trees and bushes.
The world conservation union, which determines how strongly an animal species is threatened.

gewusst: In Guinea baboons the females sometimes move from one family unit to another, which is the other way round in many other monkeys.
Baboons are among the largest monkeys that do not count as apes.
Guinea baboons have different calls with which they communicate over long distances.

teile.einleitung: The domestic cat is a small predator that has lived with humans for thousands of years. It is the most popular pet in Switzerland. Cats are skilful hunters with sharp senses who like to sleep and purr when they feel content.
wichtigste: The cat is the most popular pet in Switzerland.
The domestic cat descends from the African wildcat and was probably domesticated in the Middle East.
Cats are obligate carnivores and need animal protein.
They sleep about 12 to 16 hours a day.
Cats hear much higher sounds than humans.
A cat usually has about 4 to 6 kittens per litter.
Domestic cats can live to be about 15 to 20 years old.

abschnitte.text: The domestic cat descends from the **African wildcat**, a wild cat from Africa and Western Asia. It was probably first domesticated in the **Fertile Crescent** in the Middle East, when people settled down and stored grain. Cats hunted the mice in the stores there and so stayed close to humans. In ancient Egypt, cats were especially revered, and the goddess **Bastet** was shown with a cat's head.

Cats can retract and extend their sharp **claws**, which is why they climb trees so well. They run at up to about 48 km/h and usually land on their feet in a fall. Their eyes see much better than ours at dusk, and they hear much higher sounds than humans. With their **whiskers** they feel objects even in the dark.

Cats are **obligate carnivores**, which means that they absolutely need animal protein to survive. Certain nutrients such as taurine they have to take in with their food, because their body cannot produce them itself. Outdoor cats hunt mice, but also birds and lizards. Fresh water should always be available.

Cats sleep on average about 12 to 16 hours a day. When they feel content, they **purr**. If a cat is stressed, it often hides, eats less or grooms itself excessively. The normal body temperature of a healthy cat is about 38 to 39 degrees Celsius.

The cat is the **most popular pet** in Switzerland, and well over a million cats live here. Many of them are outdoor cats and may go outside. Vets recommend **neutering** outdoor cats so that there are not too many unwanted kittens. A cat is pregnant for about nine weeks and usually has 4 to 6 kittens, which are blind at first.

begriffe.erklaerung: A wild cat from Africa and Western Asia from which the domestic cat descends.
An animal that must eat meat to stay healthy.
A cat that is allowed to go outside on its own.
An area in the Middle East where people began farming early.

gewusst: In Cyprus a grave about 9,500 years old was found in which a human was buried together with a cat.
Cats meow mainly to talk to humans, and adult cats hardly meow at each other.
A cat usually has five toes on the front paws and four on the hind paws.

teile.einleitung: The cave hyena was a large hyena that lived in Europe and Asia during the Ice Age. It was closely related to today's spotted hyena from Africa, but somewhat bigger and stronger. Researchers find its bones and traces mainly in caves, which it used as a shelter.
wichtigste: The cave hyena belonged to the animal world of the Ice Age in Europe.
It was closely related to today's spotted hyena.
It lived in groups and used caves as a den.
With its strong jaws it could crack bones.
It hunted large animals and also ate carrion.
Towards the end of the last Ice Age it died out.

abschnitte.text: The **cave hyena** was a predator of the Ice Age and belongs to the same genus as the spotted hyena. Some researchers see it as a subspecies of the spotted hyena, others as a species of its own. It had long front legs, a sloping back and a very powerful head. Probably its coat was spotted, as in today's spotted hyenas.

The cave hyena lived in the **mammoth steppe**, a cold, grassy landscape that stretched from Western Europe to Asia. Mammoths, woolly rhinoceroses, wild horses and reindeer lived there too. Its neighbours and competitors were cave lions, cave bears, wolves and the Neanderthals. In Central Europe, too, its bones have been discovered at many sites.

Cave hyenas probably hunted wild horses, reindeer and sometimes even young woolly rhinoceroses in groups. They also ate the remains of dead animals, that is **carrion**. With their broad cheek teeth and strong chewing muscles they could crush even thick bones. In this way they used almost everything from their prey, including the bone marrow.

Cave hyenas often brought their prey into caves, where they raised their young. That is why researchers find piles of gnawed bones with bite marks there. Famous is Kirkdale Cave in England, which was investigated in 1821 and was full of hyena bones. Fossilised dung, so-called **coprolites**, also reveals what the animals ate.

The cave hyena disappeared from Europe towards the end of the last Ice Age. It probably had problems because the climate changed and its prey animals became rarer. Possibly competition with humans also played a part. Its close relative, the spotted hyena, still lives in Africa today.

begriffe.erklaerung: A long, cold period in which large parts of the Earth were covered with ice.
The flesh of dead animals.
Fossilised dung of animals from earlier times.
A cold grassland of the Ice Age in which mammoths lived.

gewusst: The caves in which hyenas lived were often veritable bone stores.
The cave hyena and the Neanderthal sometimes competed for the same caves.
The closest living relative of the cave hyena is the spotted hyena in Africa.

teile.einleitung: A locust plague arises when certain species of grasshopper multiply in huge numbers and move across the land in enormous swarms. Such swarms can consist of billions of animals and strip whole harvests bare in a short time. An old story in the Bible already tells of a plague of locusts in Egypt.
wichtigste: A locust plague is the mass appearance of locusts in large swarms.
The best-known plague species is the desert locust from Africa and Asia.
A swarm can consist of billions of animals.
Each locust eats about its own weight in plants per day.
Swarms can fly over a hundred kilometres in a day.
In the Bible, the plague of locusts is one of the ten plagues of Egypt.
Today an international early-warning system warns of new swarms.

abschnitte.text: People speak of a **locust plague** when locusts appear in such great numbers that they destroy fields and pastures. A few species are responsible, which are called **migratory locusts**. The most important is the desert locust, which occurs in North Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. Ordinary meadow grasshoppers from Switzerland do not form such swarms.

Mostly, migratory locusts live singly and inconspicuously. After a lot of rain, many plants suddenly grow in the desert and the animals multiply strongly. When they then live close together and constantly touch each other, they change: they get a different colour, become more restless and seek the closeness of the others. This change from a single animal to a **swarm animal** is called phase change.

A single swarm can be many square kilometres in size and consist of billions of animals. Each desert locust weighs only about two grams, but eats daily about as much as it weighs itself. Together, a swarm eats as much food in a day as thousands of people. With the wind, the swarms often fly over a hundred kilometres a day.

In the Bible, the Book of **Exodus** tells how locusts came over Egypt as the eighth of ten plagues. In Central Europe, too, there used to be plagues of the European migratory locust, which no longer occurs today. In North America in 1875, a huge swarm of the Rocky Mountain locust passed over the land. This species became extinct a few decades later.

From 2019 to 2021, enormous swarms passed through East Africa, Yemen, Pakistan and India. In countries such as Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia they threatened the food supply of millions of people. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the **FAO**, monitors the locusts with satellites and reports from the ground. In this way countries can fight the animals early, for example with sprays or with fungi that make only locusts ill.

begriffe.erklaerung: A species of grasshopper that under certain conditions forms huge swarms.
A very large group of animals travelling together.
The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization.
The transformation of a locust living singly into a swarm animal.

gewusst: A swarm of locusts can be so dense that it darkens the sun.
In some countries, locusts are collected from swarms and eaten.
Of all species, the Rocky Mountain locust, which once formed the largest swarms, is extinct today.

teile.einleitung: Camels are a family of mammals that includes the humped camels of the deserts and the llamas and alpacas from South America. They are true survival artists and cope with heat, cold and little water. For thousands of years they have carried people and loads and provided milk, meat and wool.
wichtigste: The family is called the camels or camelids (Camelidae).
The Old World camels include the dromedary and the Bactrian camel.
The llama, alpaca, guanaco and vicuña form the New World camels in South America.
The dromedary has one hump, the Bactrian camel two.
In the hump camels store fat, not water.
Camels have a stomach with three chambers and chew their food again.
They have two toes on each foot and walk on soft foot pads.

abschnitte.text: The **camels** include six species in two groups. The **Old World camels** live in Africa and Asia: the one-humped dromedary, the two-humped Bactrian camel and the rare wild Bactrian camel. The **New World camels** come from South America: the llama, alpaca, guanaco and vicuña. New World camels have no humps, but are closely related to the humped camels.

Camels have only **two toes** on each foot, with small, nail-like hooves. The real load is carried by a broad, soft **foot pad** that does not sink into the sand. Their upper lip is split and very mobile, so they can grasp even thorny plants. Bactrian camels have thick calluses on the chest and knees that cushion them when they lie down on hot or hard ground. When lying down, a camel folds its front legs first.

In its hump a camel stores **fat** as an energy reserve, not water, as is often believed. Camels can go several days or even weeks without drinking, losing a lot of body weight in the process. When they find water, they drink over 100 litres in a few minutes. Their body temperature may rise sharply during the day, so they sweat less and save water. Long eyelashes and nostrils that can be closed protect them from sand.

Camels eat grasses, leaves, twigs and even prickly desert plants. They have a stomach with **three chambers**, as do alpacas and llamas. Like cows, they bring their food back up and chew it again, so they are **ruminants**. But because they are built differently from cattle, they are placed in a group of their own, the tylopods.

Camels live in groups and are usually calm and patient. When they feel threatened or annoyed, they can **spit**, usually a gush of saliva and stomach contents. Llamas and alpacas spit mainly at one another, for example in quarrels over food. When walking, camels move both legs on one side of the body at the same time, which is called **pacing**.
