Almost all the golden hamsters that live in children's bedrooms today descend from these few animals. Wild golden hamsters have meanwhile become rare and endangered.

Golden hamsters are **omnivores** and eat grain, seeds, vegetables, herbs and also insects. With their stretchy **cheek pouches**, which reach as far as the shoulders, they carry food to their hiding place. There they lay up stores, which they hide well. A hamster with full cheeks looks almost twice as wide. It always needs fresh water, best from a drinking bottle or a heavy bowl.

Golden hamsters are **nocturnal** and sleep in their nest by day. Anyone who wakes them in the daytime stresses them. They live as **loners** and defend their territory, and two adult hamsters in one cage can injure each other badly. When a hamster is frightened, it often stands up on its hind legs, shows its teeth and hisses. Because they see badly, they recognise their surroundings mainly by smell and sounds.

A golden hamster needs a large enclosure with deep bedding for digging, a little house and a large running wheel. The cage should be cleaned regularly so that the hamster stays healthy, but without taking away all the stores. Bathing in water is not necessary, because the hamster cleans itself and could catch a chill and get stressed. Hamsters are small escape artists and slip out through astonishingly small holes. They are only conditionally suitable for small children, because they sleep by day and can bite if they are pestered.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mammal with particularly strong gnawing teeth that keep growing, such as a mouse, hamster or beaver.
Stretchy sacs of skin in the mouth in which the hamster carries food.
An animal that is awake at night and sleeps by day.
An animal that prefers to live alone.

gewusst: A golden hamster mother is pregnant for only about 16 days, which is one of the shortest pregnancies among mammals.
In one night a hamster can cover several kilometres in its running wheel.
No wild golden hamster lives in Switzerland, but in parts of Europe there is its larger relative, the European hamster.

teile.einleitung: Graubünden, also called the Grisons, is the largest canton of Switzerland and a paradise for wild animals. Here lie the Swiss National Park, countless mountain valleys and high peaks. The ibex on its coat of arms shows how closely Graubünden is connected with its wildlife.
wichtigste: At about 7,100 square kilometres, Graubünden is the largest canton of Switzerland by area.
It is the only canton with three official languages: German, Romansh and Italian.
The ibex is especially well known as the heraldic animal of Graubünden.
In the canton lies the Swiss National Park, which was founded in 1914.
In 2012 the first wolf pack in Switzerland for over a hundred years lived in Graubünden.
Bear, bearded vulture and red deer are also at home here again.
The capital of the canton is Chur.

abschnitte.text: Graubünden lies in the south-east of Switzerland and borders Austria, Liechtenstein and Italy. At about 7,100 square kilometres it covers around a sixth of Switzerland and consists almost entirely of mountains and **valleys**. Here the Rhine and the Inn rise, and the Inn flows through the **Engadine**. Well-known peaks are Piz Bernina at over 4,000 metres and the Tödi on the border with Glarus. Graubünden has around 150 valleys and over 600 lakes.

The **ibex** is the best-known heraldic animal of Graubünden and adorns the cantonal coat of arms. In the 19th century it had been wiped out in Switzerland by hunting. From 1911, ibex from the Italian Gran Paradiso area were reintroduced, and in 1920 also at Piz Ela in Graubünden. Today thousands of ibex live in the canton again. It is a symbol that conservation can be successful.

At Zernez in the Engadine lies the **Swiss National Park**, which was founded in 1914 as the first national park in the Alps. It is about 170 square kilometres in size, and nature may develop there entirely freely. There is no hunting, no mowing and no felling of timber. Walkers may not leave the paths. This way you can watch red deer, chamois, marmots, golden eagles and bearded vultures there.

abschnitte.titel: The return of the large animals
abschnitte.text: In Graubünden many animals that had disappeared are returning. In the National Park, **bearded vultures** were released again from 1991, and today they breed in the mountains of Graubünden. In 2005 a bear came from Italy into the Val Müstair for the first time again, after the last Swiss bear had been shot in the Lower Engadine in 1904. On the Calanda near Chur, the first **wolf pack** in Switzerland formed in 2012. The return of the wolf also leads to conflicts with sheep and goat keepers, however.

About 200,000 people live in Graubünden (as of 2023), and the capital is **Chur**, one of the oldest towns in Switzerland. The canton is the only trilingual canton: people speak German, **Romansh** and Italian. Graubünden has belonged to Switzerland since 1803. Important are tourism in places such as St. Moritz, Davos or Flims, agriculture and hydropower. The Rhaetian Railway with the Albula and Bernina lines is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

begriffe.erklaerung: One of the 26 member states of Switzerland with its own government.
An animal that is shown on the coat of arms of a country or canton.
A large protected area in which nature may develop freely.
A language of its own that is spoken mainly in Graubünden.

gewusst: Almost all the ibex of the Alps descend from a few animals that had survived in Italy.
In summer, several thousand red deer live in the Swiss National Park.
The bearded vulture, which breeds again in Graubünden, can span almost three metres with its wings.
